title: Aortic valve surgery and survival in patients with moderate or severe aortic stenosis and left ventricular dysfunction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre echocardiographic database cohort; 1634 patients had moderate (N = 1090, 67%) or severe (N = 544, 33%) AS by mean gradient criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with selection into surgery and a single-centre source; confounding by indication is likely despite inverse probability weighting.
appraisal.one_line: Duke echocardiography cohort links aortic valve replacement to lower mortality in moderate or severe AS with LV systolic dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: AVR ± CABG compared with medical therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality [hazard ratio, HR = 0.49 (0.38, 0.62), P < 0.0001].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the intervention decision in moderate AS with LV dysfunction, where trial evidence is lacking.

title: Outcomes in Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Left Main Stenting: The TAVR-LM Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective registry; 204 patients undergoing TAVR plus LM PCI, with 128 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective and non-randomised, with small subgroups and wide uncertainty in the unplanned-PCI comparison.
appraisal.one_line: First registry of TAVR combined with left main PCI reports mortality similar to matched TAVR-alone controls.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year mortality (9.4% vs. 10.2%, p = 0.83) was similar between the TAVR plus LM PCI cohort and matched controls.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a percutaneous strategy for TAVI candidates with left main disease and flags higher risk after unplanned PCI.

title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Dysfunctional Surgical Bioprosthetic Valves: An International, Multicenter Registry Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre registry; 156 patients with bioprosthetic TV dysfunction.
appraisal.main_limitation: Uncontrolled, heterogeneous registry with a young median age (40 years) and a median follow-up of 13.3 months.
appraisal.one_line: International registry of transcatheter valve-in-valve implantation within failed surgical tricuspid bioprostheses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among 152 patients in whom TVIV was attempted with a Melody (n=94) or Sapien (n=58) valve, implantation was successful in 150, with few serious complications.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest series supporting tricuspid valve-in-valve as an alternative to reoperation.

title: Should Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Be Performed in Nonagenarians?: Insights From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis of 24,025 patients in 329 hospitals, of whom 3,773 (15.7%) were aged 90 years or older.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry without a medical therapy or surgical comparator, subject to selection.
appraisal.one_line: Registry comparison of outcomes after TAVR in nonagenarians and younger patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were significantly higher among nonagenarians (age ≥90 years vs. <90 years: 30-day: 8.8% vs. 5.9%; p < 0.001; 1 year: 24.8% vs. 22.0%; p < 0.001). There were no differences in the rates of stroke, aortic valve reintervention, or myocardial infarction at 30 days or 1 year.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs selection of very elderly patients for TAVR in routine practice.

title: Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic-Valve Replacement in Intermediate-Risk Patients.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 2032 intermediate-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis at 57 centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded, with a 2-year primary end point; procedural trade-offs differed between arms (vascular complications and paravalvular regurgitation more frequent with TAVR).
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of TAVR versus surgical aortic-valve replacement in intermediate-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier event rates were 19.3% in the TAVR group and 21.1% in the surgery group (hazard ratio in the TAVR group, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.09; P=0.25).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It extends transcatheter valve replacement from high-risk to intermediate-risk patients, a large population, and bears on guideline recommendations for TAVR versus surgery.

title: 3-Year Outcomes in High-Risk Patients Who Underwent Surgical or Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 797 patients randomised at 45 U.S. centers; 750 had an attempted procedure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Analysis restricted to patients with an attempted procedure, and the abstract gives no confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year outcomes of a randomised comparison of self-expanding TAVR and surgery in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Three-year all-cause mortality or stroke was significantly lower in TAVR patients (37.3% vs. 46.7% in SAVR; p = 0.006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It shows that the benefit of TAVR over surgery in high-risk patients was sustained at 3 years.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement versus surgical valve replacement in intermediate-risk patients: a propensity score analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Cross-study propensity score analysis; 963 patients treated with SAPIEN 3 TAVR and 747 with surgical valve replacement were included.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison across two studies with differing periods, so unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity comparison of SAPIEN 3 TAVR with surgery from PARTNER 2A in intermediate-risk patients, suggesting superiority for a composite endpoint.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR was both non-inferior (pooled weighted proportion difference of -9·2%; 90% CI -12·4 to -6; p<0·0001) and superior (-9·2%, 95% CI -13·0 to -5·4; p<0·0001) to surgical valve replacement.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informed the extension of TAVR to intermediate-risk patients ahead of randomised evidence.

title: Impact of New-Onset Left Bundle Branch Block and Periprocedural Permanent Pacemaker Implantation on Clinical Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational data; 17 studies, including 4756 patients (8 studies) and 7032 patients (11 studies).
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled observational studies with heterogeneous definitions and follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis linking new-onset LBBB after TAVR with later pacemaker need and cardiac death.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: New-onset LBBB post-TAVR was associated with a higher risk of PPI (risk ratio [RR], 2.18; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.28-3.70) and cardiac death (RR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.04-1.86) during follow-up, as well with a tendency toward an increase in all-cause mortality (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.98-1.50).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Conduction disturbance is a major determinant of TAVR outcomes and device choice, and this pooled estimate frames follow-up strategies.

title: Outcomes of transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation at hospitals with and without on-site cardiac surgery department: insights from the prospective German aortic valve replacement quality assurance registry (AQUA) in 17 919 patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective national quality registry; 17 919 patients, of whom 1332 (7.4%) were treated at hospitals without on-site cardiac surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcomes only, in a registry with non-randomised site allocation.
appraisal.one_line: German AQUA registry comparison of transfemoral TAVI at hospitals with and without on-site cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Complications, including strokes (2.6 vs. 2.3%, P = 0.452) and in-hospital mortality (3.8 vs. 4.2%, P = 0.396), were similar in both groups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on guideline requirements for on-site surgery in TAVI services.

title: Two-Year Outcomes in Patients With Severe Aortic Valve Stenosis Randomized to Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: The All-Comers Nordic Aortic Valve Intervention Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial from 3 centres in Denmark and Sweden; Two-hundred eighty patients randomized to either TAVR (n=145) or SAVR (n=135).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample from three centres, underpowered for clinical endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year results of an all-comers randomised trial of TAVR versus SAVR found no difference in mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in all-cause mortality at 2 years between TAVR and SAVR (8.0% versus 9.8%, respectively; P=0.54) or cardiovascular mortality (6.5% versus 9.1%; P=0.40). The composite outcome of all-cause mortality, stroke, or myocardial infarction was also similar (15.8% versus 18.8%, P=0.43).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence in low and intermediate risk patients, contributing to later evidence synthesis on TAVR versus SAVR.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation vs. surgical aortic valve replacement for treatment of severe aortic stenosis: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of four trials including 3806 participants (TAVI n = 1898, SAVR n = 1908).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup findings by access route and sex rest on interaction tests of modest strength and trial-level data.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four randomised trials found lower 2-year all-cause death with TAVI than with SAVR, with heterogeneity by access route and sex.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVI when compared with SAVR was associated with a significant 13% relative risk reduction [hazard ratio (95% CI): 0.87 (0.76-0.99); P = 0.038]
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pooled evidence across risk strata informs the choice between TAVI and SAVR, particularly for transfemoral access.

title: Von Willebrand Factor Multimers during Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort with a validation cohort; 183 patients undergoing TAVR, plus 201 in the second cohort.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small cohort with a diagnostic accuracy focus and no test-guided intervention trial.
appraisal.one_line: von Willebrand factor multimer defects and a point-of-care test detect post-TAVR aortic regurgitation and relate to mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A CT-ADP value of more than 180 seconds had sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value of 92.3%, 92.4%, and 98.6%, respectively, for aortic regurgitation.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Offers a procedural monitor for paravalvular leak during TAVR.

title: Effect of a Cerebral Protection Device on Brain Lesions Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Severe Aortic Stenosis: The CLEAN-TAVI Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised single-centre trial, 100 enrolled patients (50 per group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single centre with a surrogate imaging endpoint; clinical neurological benefit untested.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre randomised trial in which a cerebral protection filter during TAVI was associated with fewer new MRI brain lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: the number of new lesions was lower in the filter group, 4.00 (interquartile range [IQR], 3.00-7.25) vs 10.00 (IQR, 6.75-17.00) in the control group (difference, 5.00 [IQR, 2.00-8.00]; P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports larger trials of cerebral protection with clinical endpoints.

title: Association Between Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Subsequent Infective Endocarditis and In-Hospital Death.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre international registry; 250 cases of infective endocarditis in 20 006 patients after TAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Case-based registry with no matched controls for the outcome analysis.
appraisal.one_line: International registry of infective endocarditis after TAVR gives incidence, predictors and in-hospital mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Incidence, 1.1% per person-year; 95% CI, 1.1%-1.4%. The in-hospital mortality rate was 36% (95% CI, 30.0%-41.9%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines a serious late complication of TAVR and its risk factors.

title: Transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients with severe aortic stenosis at low and intermediate risk: systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 trials with 3179 patients and a median follow-up of two years.
appraisal.main_limitation: No study reported long-term follow-up, so structural valve deterioration could not be assessed.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis in low- and intermediate-risk aortic stenosis reported absolute effects of transfemoral and transapical TAVI against SAVR, graded for certainty.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with SAVR, transfemoral TAVI was associated with reduced mortality (risk difference per 1000 patients: -30, 95% confidence interval -49 to -8, moderate certainty), stroke (-20, -37 to 1, moderate certainty)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives absolute risk differences suited to shared decision making and guideline development.

title: Late Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in High-Risk Patients: The FRANCE-2 Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective national registry; 4,201 patients enrolled in 34 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early-generation devices and a high-risk population limit applicability to current practice.
appraisal.one_line: FRANCE-2 reports late outcomes after TAVR across a national registry with median follow-up of 3.8 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 3-year all-cause mortality was 42.0% and cardiovascular mortality was 17.5%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest late-outcome dataset in early TAVR, showing stable valve performance.

title: Neurological Outcomes With Embolic Protection Devices in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Four randomized clinical trials (total n = 252).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trials with imaging surrogate endpoints and underpowered for clinical stroke.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of cerebral embolic protection during TAVR showing fewer new ischaemic lesions on imaging.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of EP was associated with lower total lesion volume (standardized mean difference -0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.06 to -0.25; p = 0.002); risk for overt stroke and all-cause mortality were nonsignificantly lower in the EP group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It frames the case for an adequately powered trial of embolic protection in TAVR with clinical endpoints.

title: Protection Against Cerebral Embolism During Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 363 patients randomised across 19 centres (safety arm n = 123, device imaging n = 121, control imaging n = 119).
appraisal.main_limitation: Not powered for clinical neurological outcomes; efficacy endpoint is imaging-based.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised evaluation of a cerebral embolic protection filter during TAVR met its safety goal but did not show a significant reduction in new lesion volume.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: New lesion volume was 178.0 mm3 in control subjects and 102.8 mm3 in the device arm (p = 0.33).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Cerebral embolic protection is used in practice without proof of clinical benefit.

title: 2016 Annual Report of The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry annual report; 54,782 patients with transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive report without adjustment for case-mix change or causal inference.
appraisal.one_line: Annual TVT Registry report describing US transcatheter aortic and mitral valve procedure trends and outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Observed in-hospital mortality decreased from 5.7% to 2.9%, and 1-year mortality decreased from 25.8% to 21.6%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents practice trends including a rise in pacemaker insertion.

title: Transcaval Access and Closure for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Prospective Investigation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre single-arm trial; 100 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design with no comparator and common bleeding and vascular complications.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective single-arm trial of transcaval access for TAVR in patients without femoral access.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Transcaval access was successful in 99 of 100 patients.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a fully percutaneous alternative to transthoracic access.

title: Surgical or Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement in Intermediate-Risk Patients.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1746 patients randomised at 87 centres; Bayesian noninferiority analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded and limited to a single self-expanding prosthesis; follow-up of 24 months says little about durability.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of self-expanding TAVR with surgical replacement in intermediate-risk severe aortic stenosis found TAVR noninferior at 24 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 24 months, the estimated incidence of the primary end point was 12.6% in the TAVR group and 14.0% in the surgery group (95% credible interval [Bayesian analysis] for difference, -5.2 to 2.3%; posterior probability of noninferiority, >0.999).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends TAVR as an alternative to surgery to intermediate-risk patients, a large population in which guideline recommendations are determined by this evidence.

title: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis in surgical and transcatheter bioprosthetic aortic valves: an observational study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled observational analysis of two registries (RESOLVE and SAVORY), 931 patients had CT imaging and 890 had interpretable scans.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised antithrombotic allocation with CT at varying intervals after implantation.
appraisal.one_line: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis on CT was more frequent after TAVR than SAVR and was less frequent with anticoagulation than with DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 106 (12%) of 890 patients had subclinical leaflet thrombosis, including five (4%) of 138 with thrombosis of surgical valves versus 101 (13%) of 752 with thrombosis of transcatheter valves (p=0·001); thrombosis was less frequent with anticoagulants (eight [4%] of 224) than with dual antiplatelet therapy (31 [15%] of 208; p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic choice after bioprosthetic aortic valve implantation and the leaflet thrombosis debate.

title: Outcomes in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Bicuspid Versus Tricuspid Aortic Valve Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre registry, 561 bicuspid and 4,546 tricuspid patients, 546 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, mostly early-generation devices, and propensity matching cannot remove residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched registry comparison found lower device success but similar 2-year mortality with TAVR in bicuspid versus tricuspid stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bicuspid AS had more frequent conversion to surgery (2.0% vs. 0.2%; p = 0.006) and lower device success (85.3% vs. 91.4%; p = 0.002); 2-year all-cause mortality was comparable (17.2% vs. 19.4%; p = 0.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the largest outcome signal for TAVR in bicuspid anatomy, a group excluded from pivotal trials.

title: Prognostic Implications of Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Patients With Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentre cohort from 4 institutions, 305 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective, small, with no comparison group managed differently.
appraisal.one_line: Patients with moderate aortic stenosis and LV systolic dysfunction had a high rate of death, valve replacement and heart failure hospitalisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 4-year follow-up, the primary composite endpoint occurred in 61%; the rate of all-cause death was 36%; AVR occurred in 24% of patients.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Highlights a population in which the benefit of earlier valve intervention for moderate stenosis is unproven.

title: Aspirin Versus Aspirin Plus Clopidogrel as Antithrombotic Treatment Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With a Balloon-Expandable Valve: The ARTE (Aspirin Versus Aspirin + Clopidogrel Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised controlled trial of 222 patients, 111 allocated to DAPT and 111 to SAPT, stopped after inclusion of 74% of the planned population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered and stopped early, with no effect estimate and confidence interval for the primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Small randomised trial of aspirin alone versus aspirin plus clopidogrel after balloon-expandable TAVR, stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite of death, MI, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or major or life-threatening bleeding tended to occur more frequently in the DAPT group (15.3% vs. 7.2%, p = 0.065). DAPT was associated with a higher rate of major or life-threatening bleeding events (10.8% vs. 3.6% in the SAPT group, p = 0.038).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence that single antiplatelet therapy is a reasonable default after TAVR, with less bleeding.

title: Procedural Experience for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Relation to Outcomes: The STS/ACC TVT Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: STS/ACC TVT Registry analysis, 42,988 commercial procedures at 395 hospitals, 2011 to 2015.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational and cannot separate learning curve from volume-outcome effect.
appraisal.one_line: US registry data linked greater hospital TAVR experience with lower risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality, bleeding and vascular complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Increasing site volume was associated with lower in-hospital risk-adjusted outcomes, including mortality (p < 0.02), vascular complications (p < 0.003), and bleeding (p < 0.001) but was not associated with stroke (p = 0.14).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs centre volume requirements and systems of care for TAVR.

title: Structural valve deterioration after transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies: Thirteen studies including 8914 patients, with median follow-up between 1.6 and 5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with inconsistent SVD definitions and follow-up of no more than five years.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review of observational studies on structural valve deterioration after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The pooled incidence of SVD was 28.08 per 10 000 patients/year (95% CI 2.46 to 73.44 per 100 patient years). Of those who developed SVD, 12% underwent valve re-intervention.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses durability, the main concern as TAVI extends to younger and lower-risk patients.

title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Outcomes Following Permanent Pacemaker Implantation After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis and meta-regression of studies comparing patients with and without PPM after TAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparisons subject to confounding, with the number of studies not stated in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of clinical and echocardiographic outcomes in patients who need a permanent pacemaker after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with and without PPM had similar all-cause mortality (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.70-1.03) at 30 days and at 1 year (RR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.92-1.16). The improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction was significantly greater in the patients without PPM (standardized mean difference, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.12-0.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the clinical consequence of conduction disturbance after TAVR, a common complication.

title: Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: Propensity-Matched Comparison.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational registry cohort linked to Medicare claims; 9,464 propensity-matched intermediate- and high-risk U.S. patients; 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with residual confounding despite propensity matching, and follow-up limited to 1 year.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched registry comparison of TAVR and SAVR in intermediate- and high-risk patients using linked registry and Medicare claims data.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR and SAVR patients experienced no difference in 1-year rates of death (17.3% vs. 17.9%; hazard ratio: 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.83 to 1.04) and stroke (4.2% vs. 3.3%; hazard ratio: 1.18; 95% CI: 0.95 to 1.47).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives real-world 1-year outcomes in a nationally representative cohort, supporting the transportability of trial results in intermediate- and high-risk patients.

title: Effect of Cerebral Embolic Protection Devices on CNS Infarction in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized clinical trial at 18 North American centres; 383 randomized patients (118 suction-based extraction, 133 intra-aortic filtration, 132 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surgical rather than transcatheter setting, and the trial was not powered for clinical stroke or delirium.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of two cerebral embolic protection devices against a standard cannula during surgical aortic valve replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of freedom from CNS infarction at 7 days was 32.0% with suction-based extraction vs 33.3% with control (between-group difference, -1.3%; 95% CI, -13.8% to 11.2%) and 25.6% with intra-aortic filtration vs 32.4% with control (between-group difference, -6.9%; 95% CI, -17.9% to 4.2%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The devices did not reduce CNS infarction, which tempers expectations for embolic protection in valve procedures.

title: Conscious Sedation Versus General Anesthesia for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Insights from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: STS/ACC TVT Registry, 1737/10 997 (15.8%) cases under conscious sedation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised allocation, with residual confounding possible despite falsification analyses.
appraisal.one_line: US registry analysis associated conscious sedation with lower mortality than general anaesthesia for transfemoral TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After inverse probability of treatment-weighted adjustment for 51 covariates, conscious sedation was associated with a reduced rate of mortality at the in-hospital (1.5% versus 2.4%, P<0.001) and 30-day (2.3% versus 4.0%, P<0.001) time points, and lower procedural success (97.9% versus 98.6%, P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports conscious sedation as a default approach and bears on a randomisable procedural choice.

title: Does mild paravalvular regurgitation post transcatheter aortic valve implantation affect survival? A meta-analysis.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 25 articles including total of 21,018 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled observational hazard ratios with significant heterogeneity and unadjusted confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating mild paravalvular regurgitation after TAVI with higher mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality HR 1.26, 95%CI 1.11-1.43 for mild PVR versus none/trivial PVR; cardiovascular mortality HR 1.28, 95%CI 1.05-1.57.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Mild PVR is common after TAVI and the abstract states that benefit of intervening on it is undetermined.

title: Long-Term Outcomes With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Women Compared With Men: Evidence From a Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Seventeen studies (8 TAVR registries; 47,188 patients; 49.4% women).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with differing baseline risk and DerSimonian-Laird random effects.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating female sex with lower long-term mortality after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality at 1 year risk ratio: 0.85; 95% confidence interval: 0.79 to 0.91 for women versus men.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies conflicting sex differences in TAVR outcomes, with more early vascular complications but lower late mortality in women.

title: Transapical Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Is Associated With Increased Cardiac Mortality in Patients With Left Ventricular Dysfunction: Insights From the PARTNER I Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of 2,084 subjects, 1,057 of whom underwent TA TAVR, adjusted for propensity of TA access.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised access comparison within a trial with residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: PARTNER I post hoc analysis associating transapical TAVR with higher mortality in patients with LV dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 2-year all-cause mortality with LV dysfunction HRadjusted: 1.52; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.12 to 2.07; p = 0.008 for transapical access.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports transfemoral access over transapical in patients with reduced ejection fraction.

title: Bioprosthetic aortic valve leaflet thrombosis detected by multidetector computed tomography is associated with adverse cerebrovascular events: a meta-analysis of observational studies.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of six studies with 11.6% (198/1,704) of patients having MDCT-defined LT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational studies, small number of studies, no randomised allocation of leaflet thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating CT-detected bioprosthetic valve leaflet thrombosis with cerebrovascular events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cerebrovascular events odds ratio [OR] 3.38, 95% CI: 1.78-6.41, p<0.001 in patients with LT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the debate on clinical relevance of subclinical leaflet thrombosis and antithrombotic strategy after valve replacement.

title: Effect of Mechanically Expanded vs Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Mortality and Major Adverse Clinical Events in High-Risk Patients With Aortic Stenosis: The REPRISE III Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial at 55 centers; 912 patients with high or extreme risk and severe, symptomatic aortic stenosis (607 mechanically expanded valve, 305 self-expanding valve); 2:1 randomisation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in high-risk patients, with higher rates of pacemaker implantation and valve thrombosis in the mechanically expanded arm.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of a mechanically expanded transcatheter valve against a self-expanding valve in high-risk aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety composite end point at 30 days occurred in 20.3% of MEV patients and 17.2% of SEV patients (difference, 3.1%; Farrington-Manning 97.5% CI, -∞ to 8.3%; P = .003 for noninferiority). At 1 year, the primary effectiveness composite end point occurred in 15.4% with the MEV and 25.5% with the SEV (difference, -10.1%; Farrington-Manning 97.5% CI, -∞ to -4.4%; P<.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It compares two transcatheter valve platforms head to head, showing a trade-off between less paravalvular leak and more conduction disturbance.

title: Transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients at low surgical risk: A meta-analysis of randomized trials and propensity score matched observational studies.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Six studies (2 RCTs and 4 PSM studies) totaling 3,484 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixes randomised and propensity-matched studies with limited follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of TAVR versus SAVR in low-risk patients with a signal of higher intermediate-term mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Intermediate-term mortality RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.11-1.89, P = 0.006 for TAVR versus SAVR; short-term mortality RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.56-1.41, P = 0.62.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses low-risk TAVR, a growing indication.

title: Dobutamine Stress Echocardiography for Management of Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective cohort, One hundred eighty-six patients with low-LVEF low-flow, low-gradient AS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Reference standard available in a subset only and observational prognostic data.
appraisal.one_line: Guideline dobutamine echocardiography criteria for true-severe low-flow, low-gradient AS had limited accuracy, whereas projected valve area performed better.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Peak stress MG ≥40 mm Hg, peak stress AVA ≤1 cm2, and the combination correctly classified AS severity in 48%, 60%, and 47% of patients, respectively, whereas AVAProj ≤1 cm2 gave 70% correct classification; AVAProj ≤1 cm2 predicted mortality under medical management (hazard ratio: 3.65; p = 0.0003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges guideline criteria that determine valve replacement in low-flow, low-gradient AS.

title: Pacemaker implantation rate after transcatheter aortic valve implantation with early and new-generation devices: a systematic review.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review; 40 studies (n = 17 139) included.
appraisal.main_limitation: Narrative synthesis of widely varying rates; no pooled estimate.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review of permanent pacemaker rates after TAVI with early and new-generation prostheses and the factors linked to implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of a PPI after the use of a new-generation TAVI prosthesis ranged between 2.3% and 36.1%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Conduction disturbance is the main remaining procedural limitation of TAVI as it moves to younger patients.

title: Comparative analysis of cerebrovascular events in transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of five RCT with a total of 5,414 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial populations and valve platforms differ, with definitions of stroke varying.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials finding comparable cerebrovascular events after TAVR and SAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All strokes at one year RR 0.92, 95% CI: 0.69-1.22; major stroke RR 0.92, 95% CI: 0.62-1.37.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consolidates randomised stroke data across TAVR versus SAVR trials.

title: Impact of anticoagulation therapy on valve haemodynamic deterioration following transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre study of 2466 patients with propensity matching of 622 patients per group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with haemodynamic rather than clinical endpoint; few received direct oral anticoagulants.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre cohort associating anticoagulation after TAVR with less valve haemodynamic deterioration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: VHD was significantly lower in the AC group (0.6%) compared with the non-AC group (3.7%, P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to antithrombotic therapy after TAVR and durability.

title: Comparison of single versus dual antiplatelet therapy after TAVR: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of six studies (3 RCTs and 3 observational studies, n = 840).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small total sample with mixed randomised and observational designs.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating dual antiplatelet therapy after TAVR with more bleeding than single therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or life-threatening bleeding RR = 2.52 (95% CI 1.62-3.92, P < 0.0001) with DAPT versus SAPT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports single antiplatelet therapy after TAVR.

title: Delayed Coronary Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective international registry of 18 centres, November 2005 to December 2016; 38 DCO cases from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective case collection without a denominator for timing and subject to reporting bias.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry description of delayed coronary obstruction after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 38 DCO (incidence 0.22%) cases were identified from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures. DCO occurred more commonly after valve-in-valve procedures (0.89% vs. 0.18%; p < 0.001) and if self-expandable valves were used during the index procedure (0.36% vs. 0.11% balloon expandable; p < 0.01). The overall in-hospital death rate was 50% (n = 19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Characterises a rare, highly lethal complication relevant to coronary access planning after TAVR.

title: Standardized End Point Definitions for Coronary Intervention Trials: The Academic Research Consortium-2 Consensus Document.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Definitions are consensus-based and relevant mainly to device trial design.
appraisal.one_line: Academic Research Consortium-2 consensus on standardised endpoint definitions for coronary device trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standard endpoints shape the comparability of future stent and scaffold trials.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement of Failed Surgically Implanted Bioprostheses: The STS/ACC Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry linked to Medicare claims; ViV-TAVR (n = 1,150) matched 1:2 to NV-TAVR (n = 2,259).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised, matched comparison of groups with different risk profiles.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC registry comparison of valve-in-valve TAVR for failed surgical bioprostheses against native-valve TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted analysis revealed lower 30-day mortality (hazard ratio: 0.503; 95% confidence interval: 0.302 to 0.839; p = 0.008), lower 1-year mortality (hazard ratio: 0.653; 95% confidence interval: 0.505 to 0.844; p = 0.001), and hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio: 0.685; 95% confidence interval: 0.500 to 0.939; p = 0.019) in the ViV-TAVR group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides large real-world outcomes for valve-in-valve TAVR, supporting its use in surgical bioprosthesis failure.

title: Long-Term Mortality and Early Valve Dysfunction According to Anticoagulation Use: The FRANCE TAVI Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: FRANCE TAVI registry; 12,804 patients included, 11,469 analysed for mortality and 2,555 eligible for BVD assessment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with confounding by indication and missing data handled by imputation.
appraisal.one_line: FRANCE TAVI registry analysis of anticoagulation, mortality and bioprosthesis valve dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Anticoagulation at discharge (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.35 to 0.82; p = 0.005) and a nonfemoral approach (aOR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.28 to 1.02; p = 0.049) were independently associated with lower rates of BVD.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes to the debate on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI, where randomised data remain limited.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients With Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicenter, unblinded trial of 200 low-risk patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis at 11 centers, compared with an inverse probability weighting-adjusted control cohort of 719 patients who underwent SAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with historical controls from a registry.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm US trial of TAVR in low-risk patients compared with historical surgical controls.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, there was zero all-cause mortality in the TAVR group versus 1.7% mortality in the SAVR group. The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Early feasibility evidence for TAVR in low-risk patients ahead of randomised comparisons.

title: 5-Year Outcomes of Self-Expanding Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in High-Risk Patients.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 797 patients randomized, 750 underwent an attempted implant.
appraisal.main_limitation: Not a primary-endpoint analysis with a CI in the abstract; high-risk population only.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year results of self-expanding TAVR versus SAVR in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality rates at 5 years were 55.3% for TAVR and 55.4% for SAVR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Durability and long-term survival data for TAVI against surgery.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve replacement for degenerated bioprostheses, failed annuloplasty rings, and mitral annular calcification.

appraisal.design_and_n: TMVR multicentre registry of 521 patients (322 with ViV, 141 with ViR, 58 with ViMAC).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised registry without a surgical comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of transcatheter mitral valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring and valve-in-MAC procedures showing worse outcomes in the latter two.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality was higher after ViMAC compared with ViR and ViV at 30 days (34.5% vs. 9.9% vs. 6.2%; log-rank P < 0.001) and 1 year (62.8% vs. 30.6% vs. 14.0%; log-rank P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs patient selection for transcatheter mitral replacement in failed repairs and calcified annuli.

title: Association of Renin-Angiotensin Inhibitor Treatment With Mortality and Heart Failure Readmission in Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort of 21 312 patients who underwent TAVR at 417 US sites; 15 896 included after 1:1 propensity matching.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational; residual confounding and indication bias likely.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-Medicare linkage associating RAS inhibitor prescription after TAVR with lower mortality and heart failure readmission.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with a prescription for a RAS inhibitor vs those with no prescription had lower mortality rates at 1 year (12.5% vs 14.9%, respectively; absolute risk difference [ARD], -2.4% [95% CI, -3.5% to -1.4%]; hazard ratio [HR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.76 to 0.90]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Generates a hypothesis for post-TAVR pharmacotherapy that a randomised trial could test.

title: Five-Year Clinical Outcome and Valve Durability After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in High-Risk Patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry of 4201 patients enrolled between January 2010 and January 2012 in 34 centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: High-risk population, with echocardiographic data incomplete for structural valve deterioration.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of the FRANCE-2 national TAVR registry with hemodynamic valve deterioration data.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall, at 5 years, all-cause mortality was 60.8% (n=2478; 95% CI, 59.3% to 62.3%). The rates of severe SVD and moderate/severe SVD at 5 years were 2.5% and 13.3%, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest long-term dataset on durability in high-risk TAVR.

title: Rate of peri-procedural stroke observed with cerebral embolic protection during transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a patient-level propensity-matched analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of SENTINEL US IDE, CLEAN-TAVI and SENTINEL-Ulm; N = 1306, 533 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Propensity matching of non-randomised pooled data, and the randomised trials were not powered for stroke.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled patient-level propensity-matched analysis associated dual-filter cerebral embolic protection with lower peri-procedural stroke during TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Procedural all-stroke was lower with protection than without (1.88% vs. 5.44%, odds ratio 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.17-0.72, relative risk reduction 65%, P = 0.0028).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the debate on cerebral embolic protection in TAVR, where randomised evidence on stroke remained uncertain.

title: Comparison of balloon-expandable vs. self-expandable valves in patients undergoing transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation: from the CENTER-collaboration.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of 10 registries or trials (CENTER-collaboration); N = 12 381, 6239 with BE-valves and 6142 with SE-valves.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with propensity matching, so residual confounding by anatomy and operator choice remains.
appraisal.one_line: Large pooled propensity-matched comparison associated balloon-expandable TAVI valves with less stroke and pacemaker implantation but more bleeding in new-generation devices, without a difference in 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days mortality was not statistically different (BE: 5.3% vs. SE: 6.2%, relative risk (RR) 0.9; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.7-1.0, P = 0.10). Pacemaker implantation was lower with BE-valves (BE: 7.8% vs. SE: 20.3%, RR 0.4; 95% CI 0.3-0.4, P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest comparison of valve platforms in transfemoral TAVI, relevant to device selection.

title: Five-Year Clinical and Echocardiographic Outcomes From the NOTION Randomized Clinical Trial in Patients at Lower Surgical Risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (NOTION, NCT01057173); TAVR with self-expanding CoreValve (n=145) versus SAVR (n=135).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial at three Nordic centres with a single self-expanding valve type.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year NOTION results show no difference between TAVR and SAVR in death, stroke or myocardial infarction in lower-risk patients, with more pacemaker implantation and aortic regurgitation after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 5 years, there were no differences between TAVR and SAVR in the composite outcome (Kaplan-Meier estimates 38.0% versus 36.3%, log-rank test P=0.86). A new pacemaker was needed in 43.7% versus 8.7% (P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Among the longest randomised follow-up data for TAVR versus SAVR in lower-risk patients, relevant to durability and age thresholds.

title: Durability of Transcatheter and Surgical Bioprosthetic Aortic Valves in Patients at Lower Surgical Risk.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial follow-up (NOTION, NCT01057173); TAVR (n = 139) versus SAVR (n = 135).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with limited events and a single self-expanding valve platform.
appraisal.one_line: Six-year NOTION data show structural valve deterioration was more frequent after SAVR than TAVR with similar bioprosthetic valve failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 6 years, the rate of SVD was higher for SAVR than TAVR (24.0% vs. 4.8%; p < 0.001), whereas BVF rates were similar after SAVR and TAVR through 6 years (6.7% vs. 7.5%; p = 0.89).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides standardised durability data for TAVR in lower-risk patients, a central uncertainty for younger patients.

title: Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement with a Self-Expanding Valve in Low-Risk Patients.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial (NCT02701283); 1468 patients randomised, attempted procedure in 1403; Bayesian primary analysis when 850 patients had 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Interim Bayesian analysis with a composite of death or disabling stroke and short follow-up for valve durability.
appraisal.one_line: Self-expanding supra-annular TAVR was noninferior to surgery for death or disabling stroke at 24 months in low-surgical-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 24-month estimated incidence of the primary end point was 5.3% in the TAVR group and 6.7% in the surgery group (difference, -1.4 percentage points; 95% Bayesian credible interval for difference, -4.9 to 2.1; posterior probability of noninferiority >0.999).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends TAVR to low-risk patients, which bears directly on guideline age and risk thresholds.

title: Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement with a Balloon-Expandable Valve in Low-Risk Patients.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (PARTNER 3, NCT02675114); 1000 patients randomised at 71 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up of one year only, and the composite includes rehospitalisation.
appraisal.one_line: Balloon-expandable TAVR reduced the composite of death, stroke or rehospitalisation at one year compared with surgery in low-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the rate of the primary composite end point at 1 year was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the surgery group (8.5% vs. 15.1%; absolute difference, -6.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -10.8 to -2.5; P<0.001 for noninferiority; hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.79; P = 0.001 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports TAVR as an alternative to surgery in low-risk patients and is likely to shape guideline recommendations.

title: Procedural Volume and Outcomes for Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: TVT Registry analysis of 113,662 TAVR procedures performed at 555 hospitals by 2960 operators from 2015 through 2017.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry analysis; residual confounding and unmeasured hospital factors.
appraisal.one_line: Large US registry analysis associating lower TAVR hospital volume with higher 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted 30-day mortality was higher and more variable at hospitals in the lowest-volume quartile (3.19%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.78 to 3.67) than at hospitals in the highest-volume quartile (2.66%; 95% CI, 2.48 to 2.85) (odds ratio, 1.21; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs volume requirements and centralisation policy for TAVR programmes.

title: 3-Year Outcomes After Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Degenerated Bioprostheses: The PARTNER 2 Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicenter PARTNER 2 registries of 365 high-risk patients undergoing valve-in-valve procedures.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year outcomes of valve-in-valve TAVR for degenerated surgical bioprostheses in the PARTNER 2 registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the overall Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality was 32.7%. Aortic valve re-replacement was required in 1.9%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports durability of valve-in-valve TAVR in high-risk patients.

title: Association Between Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Bicuspid vs Tricuspid Aortic Stenosis and Mortality or Stroke.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based prospective cohort study (STS/ACC TVT Registry), 552 US centers; 81 822 patients, 2691 propensity-score matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with propensity matching, a single balloon-expandable valve platform, and no randomised comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Registry cohort associated TAVR for bicuspid stenosis with similar mortality but higher 30-day stroke and more procedural complications requiring open heart surgery than tricuspid stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality was not significantly different between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic stenosis at 30 days (2.6% vs 2.5%; hazard ratio [HR], 1.04, [95% CI, 0.74-1.47]) and 1 year (10.5% vs 12.0%; HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.10]). The 30-day stroke rate was significantly higher for bicuspid vs tricuspid aortic stenosis (2.5% vs 1.6%; HR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.06-2.33]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides large-scale data for bicuspid anatomy, which the pivotal randomised trials excluded.

title: Association Between Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Early Postprocedural Stroke.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort of 101 430 patients treated at 521 US hospitals in the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry; antithrombotic comparisons are open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: TVT Registry analysis of early stroke after TAVR showing stable rates over time.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At day 30, there were 2290 patients (2.3%) with a stroke of any kind (95% CI, 2.2%-2.4%), and 373 patients (0.4%) with transient ischemic attacks (95% CI, 0.3%-0.4%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines the benchmark for periprocedural stroke that embolic protection and antithrombotic strategies must beat.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation vs. surgical aortic valve replacement for treatment of symptomatic severe aortic stenosis: an updated meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials (PROSPERO CRD42016037273); seven trials, 8020 participants, TAVI (4014) and SAVR (4006).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level data with short follow-up and heterogeneous valve platforms and risk populations.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of seven randomised trials found TAVI associated with lower all-cause mortality and stroke than SAVR up to 2 years across surgical risk strata.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation was associated with a significant reduction of all-cause mortality compared to SAVR {hazard ratio [HR] 0.88 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.78-0.99], P = 0.030}. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation resulted in lower risk of strokes [HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.68-0.98), P = 0.028].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the low-risk trials with earlier trials to inform the TAVI versus SAVR decision across the risk spectrum.

title: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibition Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre prospective registry cohort, 10 institutions; 2,785 patients, 1,622 treated with RAS inhibitors.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with confounding by indication, and the authors describe the findings as hypothesis generating.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry cohort associated renin-angiotensin system inhibitors after TAVR with lower cardiovascular mortality and favourable left ventricular remodelling.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After adjustment for baseline differences, cardiovascular mortality at 3-year follow-up was lower (odds ratio: 0.59; 95% confidence interval: 0.41 to 0.87; p = 0.007) in patients treated with RAS inhibitors.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Generates a hypothesis for post-TAVR pharmacotherapy that an ongoing randomised trial will test.

title: Infective endocarditis after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a nationwide study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide registry cohort, 4336 patients between 2008 and mid-2018.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design, so risk factors are associations; PVE events are few.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide registry linkage estimating prosthetic valve endocarditis incidence, risk factors and survival after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk for PVE after TAVI was 1.4% (95% confidence interval 1.0-1.8%) the first year and 0.8% (0.6-1.1%) per year thereafter. One-year survival after PVE diagnosis was 58% (49-68%), and 5-year survival was 29% (17-41%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives validated nationwide incidence and prognosis for a serious late complication as TAVI moves to lower-risk patients.

title: Comparison of a Complete Percutaneous Versus Surgical Approach to Aortic Valve Replacement and Revascularization in Patients at Intermediate Surgical Risk: Results From the Randomized SURTAVI Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective randomised SURTAVI trial; 332 of 1660 patients with attempted implants were assigned to revascularisation (169 TAVR plus PCI, 163 SAVR plus CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: Revascularisation was not randomised separately and patients with SYNTAX score >22 were excluded; the subgroup is small.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified SURTAVI analysis found no difference in 2-year death or disabling stroke between TAVR plus PCI and SAVR plus CABG in intermediate-risk patients with noncomplex coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant difference in the rate of the primary end point was found between TAVR and percutaneous coronary intervention and SAVR and coronary artery bypass grafting (16.0%; 95% CI, 11.1-22.9 versus 14.0%; 95% CI, 9.2-21.1; P=0.62), or between TAVR and SAVR (11.9%; 95% CI, 9.5-14.7 versus 12.3%; 95% CI, 9.8-15.4; P=0.76).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the management of CAD in TAVI candidates, a domain where evidence from randomised comparisons is sparse.

title: Poor Long-Term Survival in Patients With Moderate Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Cohort of 122,809 male and 118,494 female patients with measured aortic valve haemodynamics, median 1,208 days follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational; untreated-patient survival may reflect comorbidity and echocardiographic selection.
appraisal.one_line: Large echocardiographic cohort showing graded mortality risk across aortic stenosis severity, including moderate AS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 5-year mortality was 56% and 67%, respectively, in those with moderate AS (mean gradient 20.0 to 39.0 mm Hg/peak velocity 3.0 to 3.9 m/s) and severe AS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the case for trials of intervention in moderate aortic stenosis.

title: Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 4 RCTs, 2,887 patients (1,497 TAVR, 1,390 SAVR), random-effects models.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only 1-year follow-up, with few deaths and a pooled evidence base of four trials with different devices.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four RCTs in low-risk patients found lower 1-year all-cause and cardiovascular death with TAVR than SAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with SAVR, TAVR was associated with significantly lower risk of all-cause death (2.1% vs. 3.5%; RR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.39 to 0.96; p = 0.03; I2 = 0%) and cardiovascular death (1.6% vs. 2.9%; RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.33 to 0.90; p = 0.02) at 1 year.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pooled low-risk TAVR evidence, relevant to guideline age thresholds, although durability beyond one year is unknown.

title: Sex Differences in Transfemoral Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of a global patient-level dataset, N = 12,381 (7,120 women, 5,261 men).
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective pooled data from 2007 to 2018 with unmeasured confounding and varying device generations.
appraisal.one_line: CENTER collaboration found similar 30-day stroke and mortality in women and men after transfemoral TAVR, with more major bleeding in women.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Both sexes had similar rates of 30-day stroke (2.3% vs. 2.5%; p = 0.53) and mortality (5.9% vs. 5.5%; p = 0.17). In contrast, women had a 50% higher risk of life-threatening or major bleeding (6.7% vs. 4.4%; p < 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Identifies bleeding as a sex-specific procedural target in TAVR.

title: Safety and efficacy of a self-expanding versus a balloon-expandable bioprosthesis for transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis: a randomised non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial at 20 centres; 739 patients (372 ACURATE neo, 367 SAPIEN 3).
appraisal.main_limitation: Thirty-day composite endpoint with a wide noninferiority margin of 7.7% and a manufacturer-funded design.
appraisal.one_line: SCOPE I found the self-expanding ACURATE neo did not meet noninferiority against the balloon-expandable SAPIEN 3 for early safety and efficacy after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Within 30 days, the primary endpoint occurred in 87 (24%) patients in the ACURATE neo and in 60 (16%) in the SAPIEN 3 group; thus, non-inferiority of the ACURATE neo was not met (absolute risk difference 7·1% [upper 95% confidence limit 12·0%], p=0·42).
appraisal.why_it_matters: One of few head-to-head randomised TAVR device comparisons, showing a difference in early valve performance.

title: Health Status After Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients With Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial substudy; 1,000 low-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis, KCCQ, SF-36 and EQ-5D at baseline, 1, 6 and 12 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label patient-reported outcomes with a shrinking difference over time.
appraisal.one_line: PARTNER 3 health status analysis found better KCCQ-OS with TAVR than surgery early, with a smaller difference at 6 and 12 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 month, TAVR was associated with better health status than surgery (mean difference in KCCQ-OS 16.0 points; p < 0.001). At 6 and 12 months, health status remained better with TAVR, although the effect was reduced (mean difference in KCCQ-OS 2.6 and 1.8 points respectively; p < 0.04 for both).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports low-risk TAVR on quality-of-life grounds, complementing the mortality evidence.

title: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis After TAVR and SAVR: Insights From the PARTNER Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled cohort of PARTNER 1 and PARTNER 2 trials and registries, 8530 patients; PVE adjudicated by a clinical events committee.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc pooling of trials and registries with few events, so risk-factor findings are associations only.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled PARTNER trial and registry analysis of prosthetic valve endocarditis incidence after TAVR and SAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PVE occurred in 107 cases (5.06 PVE events per 1000 person-years over a mean follow-up of 2.69±1.55 years [95% CI, 4.19-6.12]). The incidence of TAVR-PVE (5.21 PVE per 1000 person-years [95% CI, 4.26-6.38]) was not significantly different from SAVR-PVE (4.10 per 1000 person-years [95% CI, 2.33-7.22]; incident rate ratio, 1.27 [95% CI, 0.70-2.32]; P=0.44).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides adjudicated incidence data showing no clear difference in endocarditis between TAVR and SAVR.

title: A Controlled Trial of Rivaroxaban after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1644 patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation after successful TAVR, terminated prematurely for safety.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination limits precision and the mortality difference was not a prespecified primary outcome.
appraisal.one_line: GALILEO found a rivaroxaban-based strategy after TAVR increased death, thromboembolic events and bleeding versus antiplatelet therapy and was stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death or a first thromboembolic event had occurred in 105 patients in the rivaroxaban group and in 78 patients in the antiplatelet group (incidence rates, 9.8 and 7.2 per 100 person-years, respectively; hazard ratio with rivaroxaban, 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01 to 1.81; P = 0.04). A total of 64 deaths occurred in the rivaroxaban group and 38 in the antiplatelet group (5.8 and 3.4 per 100 person-years, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.13 to 2.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine anticoagulation after TAVR in patients without another indication, changing antithrombotic practice.

title: Early Surgery or Conservative Care for Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial, 145 asymptomatic patients (73 early surgery, 72 conservative care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, open-label single-country trial of surgical rather than transcatheter intervention in a very severe stenosis subgroup.
appraisal.one_line: RECOVERY randomised small trial found early surgery lowered operative mortality or cardiovascular death versus conservative care in asymptomatic very severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 1 patient in the early-surgery group (1%) and in 11 of 72 patients in the conservative-care group (15%) (hazard ratio, 0.09; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.01 to 0.67; P = 0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing of intervention in asymptomatic aortic stenosis and sets the stage for transcatheter trials.

title: Reduced Leaflet Motion after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised CT substudy, 231 patients enrolled; 97 rivaroxaban and 101 antiplatelet with evaluable scans.
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary endpoint is an imaging finding whose clinical meaning is unclear, in a substudy.
appraisal.one_line: GALILEO-4D found fewer reduced leaflet motion events with rivaroxaban than antiplatelet therapy after TAVR, despite worse clinical outcomes in the main trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At least one prosthetic valve leaflet with grade 3 or higher motion reduction was found in 2 of 97 patients (2.1%) who had scans that could be evaluated in the rivaroxaban group, as compared with 11 of 101 (10.9%) in the antiplatelet group (difference, -8.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -16.5 to -1.9; P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that leaflet thrombosis can be reduced pharmacologically but that this did not translate to clinical benefit.

title: Impact of Sapien 3 Balloon-Expandable Versus Evolut R Self-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Aortic Stenosis: Data From a Nationwide Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: French administrative hospital-discharge database, 31 113 patients treated 2014 to 2018; 20 918 analysed after matching (10 459 in each group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with limited clinical detail and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide French propensity-matched comparison of Sapien 3 balloon-expandable and Evolut R self-expanding TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BE TAVR was associated with a lower yearly incidence of all-cause death (relative risk, 0.88; corrected P=0.005), cardiovascular death (relative risk, 0.82; corrected P=0.002), and rehospitalization for heart failure (relative risk, 0.84; corrected P<0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the largest head-to-head comparison of two widely used TAVR platforms.

title: Balloon-Expandable Versus Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Propensity-Matched Comparison From the FRANCE-TAVI Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide registry; 12 141 patients, 3910 matched pairs of balloon-expandable and self-expanding valves.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data from 2013 to 2015 covering early-generation valves, with possible residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: FRANCE-TAVI propensity-matched analysis associated self-expanding valves with more paravalvular regurgitation and higher mortality than balloon-expandable valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the first coprimary outcome was higher with SE-THV (19.8%) compared with BE-THV (11.9%; relative risk, 1.68 [95% CI, 1.46-1.91]; P<0.0001). During follow up, all cause mortality occurred in 899 patients treated with SE-THV (2-year mortality, 29.8%) and in 801 patients treated with BE-THV (2-year mortality, 26.6%; hazard ratio, 1.17 [95% CI, 1.06-1.29]; P=0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Generates a hypothesis on valve type that randomised head-to-head trials have since tested.

title: Clinical impact of conduction disturbances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement recipients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies (7792 patients for LBBB, 42 927 for pacemaker).
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled observational studies with unadjusted confounding between conduction disturbance and baseline risk.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis linked new persistent LBBB and pacemaker implantation after TAVR to higher 1-year death and heart failure hospitalisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NOP-LBBB was associated with an increased risk of all-cause death [risk ratio (RR) 1.32, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.17-1.49; P < 0.001], cardiac death (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.20-1.78; P < 0.001), heart failure hospitalization (RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.05-1.72; P = 0.02), and PPI (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.58-2.27; P < 0.001) at 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Conduction disturbance is a key determinant of valve choice and a priority in lower-risk populations.

title: Five-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 2032 patients with severe aortic stenosis at intermediate surgical risk.
appraisal.main_limitation: More paravalvular regurgitation and reinterventions after TAVR; transthoracic access cohort fared worse.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of a randomised comparison of TAVR with surgical valve replacement at intermediate surgical risk.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, there was no significant difference in the incidence of death from any cause or disabling stroke between the TAVR group and the surgery group (47.9% and 43.4%, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.95 to 1.25; P = 0.21)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Durability and late outcomes bear directly on the choice between TAVR and surgery in intermediate-risk patients.

title: Comparison of newer generation self-expandable vs. balloon-expandable valves in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the randomized SOLVE-TAVI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, open-label, 2 x 2 factorial randomised trial; 447 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite endpoint mixes outcomes of unequal weight; stroke and leak components differed in direction.
appraisal.one_line: Equivalence trial of self-expanding versus balloon-expandable transcatheter valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite endpoint occurred in 28.4% of SEV patients and 26.1% of BEV patients meeting the prespecified criteria of equivalence [rate difference -2.39 (90% confidence interval, CI -9.45 to 4.66); Pequivalence = 0.04]
appraisal.why_it_matters: Valve platform choice is a common TAVI decision with few head-to-head randomised data.

title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease: A Report From the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry, November 2011 through November 2018; 170 959 eligible procedures, of which 5412 (3.2%) in bicuspid AV, including 3705 with current-generation devices.
appraisal.main_limitation: Registry data without randomisation; bicuspid patients were younger and lower risk, and the abstract is truncated for mortality results.
appraisal.one_line: Large national registry comparison of TAVR outcomes in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic stenosis, by device generation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: With current-generation devices, device success was slightly lower in the bicuspid (versus tricuspid) AV group (96.3% in bicuspid versus 97.4% in tricuspid, P=0.07). In bicuspid patients, current-generation devices increased device success (93.5 versus 96.3; P=0.001) and reduced 2+ aortic insufficiency (14.0% versus 2.7%; P<0.001) compared with older-generation devices.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the largest outcome dataset for TAVR in bicuspid valves, a group excluded from pivotal trials.

title: Anticoagulation with or without Clopidogrel after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 157 patients on oral anticoagulation alone and 156 on oral anticoagulation plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with a bleeding primary outcome; not powered for thromboembolic events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of oral anticoagulation with or without clopidogrel after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding occurred in 34 of the 157 patients (21.7%) receiving oral anticoagulation alone and in 54 of the 156 (34.6%) receiving oral anticoagulation plus clopidogrel (risk ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43 to 0.90; P = 0.01)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting clopidogrel in TAVI patients with an indication for anticoagulation.

title: Repeat Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Transcatheter Prosthesis Dysfunction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Redo-TAVR registry at 37 centers, 212 consecutive redo-TAVR procedures among 63,876 TAVR procedures (0.33%): 74 within and 138 beyond 1 year of the initial procedure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small non-randomised series without a comparator and with selected centres.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of redo-TAVR for transcatheter valve dysfunction with early and late failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Device success using VARC-2 criteria was achieved in 180 patients (85.1%). Survival at 30 days was 94.6% and 98.5% (p = 0.101) and 83.6% and 88.3% (p = 0.335) at 1 year for patients presenting with early and late valve dysfunction, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs lifetime management and durability planning as TAVR extends to younger patients.

title: Comparison of in-hospital outcomes and readmissions for valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement vs. reoperative surgical aortic valve replacement: a contemporary assessment of real-world outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: National Readmission Database 2012-16, VIV-TAVR (n = 3443) and isolated re-SAVR (n = 3372); 2181 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative claims data with 30-day outcomes only and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide claims comparison of valve-in-valve TAVR with reoperative SAVR for degenerated bioprosthetic aortic valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After matching (n = 2181 matched pairs), VIV-TAVR was associated with lower odds of 30-day mortality (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.23-0.74), 30-day morbidity (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.43-0.72), and major bleeding (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.85).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports VIV-TAVR over re-SAVR in a common failure scenario where randomised data are lacking.

title: Self-expanding intra-annular versus commercially available transcatheter heart valves in high and extreme risk patients with severe aortic stenosis (PORTICO IDE): a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised non-inferiority trial; 750 patients, 381 to Portico and 369 to commercial valves.
appraisal.main_limitation: Device-specific result for a first-generation valve; recruitment was paused for 11 months.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of the Portico self-expanding valve versus commercially available valves in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For the primary safety endpoint at 30 days, the event rate was higher in the Portico valve group than in the commercial valve group (52 [13·8%] vs 35 [9·6%]; absolute difference 4·2, 95% CI -0·4 to 8·8 [upper confidence bound {UCB} 8·1%]; pnon-inferiority=0·034, psuperiority=0·071)
