appraisal.why_it_matters: Valve-specific randomised data in high and extreme risk TAVR.

title: Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve Aortic Valve Replacement as an Alternative to Surgical Re-Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: French administrative hospital-discharge database 4,327 patients treated between 2010 and 2019; 717 patients analysed in each arm after matching.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with limited clinical detail and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Second nationwide French propensity-matched comparison of valve-in-valve TAVR and redo SAVR for bioprosthesis failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, VIV TAVR was associated with lower rates of the composite of all-cause mortality, all-cause stroke, myocardial infarction, and major or life-threatening bleeding (odds ratio: 0.62; 95% confidence interval: 0.44 to 0.88; p = 0.03). During follow-up (median 516 days), the combined endpoint of cardiovascular death, all-cause stroke, myocardial infarction, or rehospitalization for heart failure was not different between the 2 groups (odds ratio: 1.18; 95% confidence interval: 0.99 to 1.41; p = 0.26).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows early benefit but no difference in mid-term composite for VIV TAVR versus redo SAVR, with more HF rehospitalisation and pacing.

title: Aspirin with or without Clopidogrel after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised controlled trial; 331 patients assigned to aspirin alone and 334 to aspirin plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; ischaemic components were infrequent and the study was not powered for them.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of aspirin alone versus aspirin plus clopidogrel after TAVI in patients without an anticoagulation indication.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A bleeding event occurred in 50 patients (15.1%) receiving aspirin alone and in 89 (26.6%) receiving aspirin plus clopidogrel (risk ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.77; P = 0.001)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports single antiplatelet therapy after TAVI and is likely to inform guideline recommendations.

title: Comparison of Self-Expanding Bioprostheses for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: SCOPE 2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, multicentre trial, 23 centres, 796 patients aged 75 years or older (ACURATE neo n=398, Evolut n=398); NCT03192813.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label comparison of two devices with a non-inferiority margin that was not met; secondary findings not powered.
appraisal.one_line: SCOPE 2: the ACURATE neo did not meet non-inferiority to CoreValve Evolut for death or stroke at 1 year and showed more aortic regurgitation and cardiac death.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end point occurred in 15.8% with ACURATE neo and 13.9% with Evolut (absolute risk difference, 1.8%, upper 1-sided 95% confidence limit, 6.1%; P=0.0549 for noninferiority). New permanent pacemaker at 30 days was 10.5% versus 18.0% (absolute risk difference, -7.5% [95% CI, -12.4 to -2.60]; P=0.0027).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised head-to-head of supra-annular and intra-annular self-expanding TAVI valves; a negative result for one device with direct implications for device selection.

title: Structural Deterioration of Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Bioprostheses in the PARTNER-2 Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: PARTNER 2A randomised trial plus SAPIEN 3 registry (propensity-matched comparison); NCT01314313, NCT03222128; sample size not stated in the extracted abstract.
appraisal.main_limitation: SAPIEN 3 comparison is non-randomised and propensity-matched; 5-year follow-up is short for durability.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year structural valve deterioration was higher with SAPIEN XT than SAVR, but not different with SAPIEN 3 versus matched SAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 5-year exposure-adjusted SVD (per 100 patient-years) was 1.61 ± 0.24% versus 0.63 ± 0.16% for SAPIEN XT versus SAVR; for SAPIEN 3 versus matched SAVR, 5-year SVD was 0.68 ± 0.18% versus 0.60 ± 0.17% (p = 0.71).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs durability expectations for balloon-expandable TAVI in intermediate-risk patients.

title: 2020 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway on Management of Conduction Disturbances in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology Solution Set Oversight Committee.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus decision pathway; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations rest largely on expert opinion because adequately powered trials are absent.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC expert consensus pathway for conduction disturbances after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives a US society position on pacing after TAVI, against which ESC guidance can be compared.

title: STS-ACC TVT Registry of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: STS-ACC TVT Registry, 276 316 patients undergoing TAVR, including 8,395 low-risk patients treated in 2019.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive review without adjusted comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-wide description of US TAVR volume, risk spectrum and outcomes from 2011 to 2019, including the first low-risk cohort.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Since 2011, the 30-day mortality rate has decreased (7.2% to 2.5%), stroke has started to decrease (2.75% to 2.3%), but pacemaker need is unchanged (10.9% to 10.8%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives the national denominator and trends for TAVR practice, including pacemaker rates that remain unchanged.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Many recommendations rest on lower levels of evidence; the abstract gives no class or level detail.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary, including timing and choice of surgical and catheter interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for TAVI, mitral and tricuspid intervention decisions, to compare with ESC guidance.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Same document as the Circulation publication; recommendation levels not given in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary (JACC publication), covering diagnostic work-up and timing and choice of interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for valve intervention decisions; duplicate publication of the same guideline.

title: Transcatheter Replacement of Transcatheter Versus Surgically Implanted Aortic Valve Bioprostheses.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Redo-TAVR international registry, 434 TAV-in-TAV and 624 TAV-in-SAV procedures; 330 matched (165:165).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small matched sample and voluntary registry reporting.
appraisal.one_line: Matched redo-TAVR registry compared TAV-in-TAV with TAV-in-SAV.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Procedural success was observed in 120 (72.7%) versus 103 (62.4%) patients (p = 0.045). Mortality at 30 days was 5 (3%) after TAV-in-TAV and 7 (4.4%) after TAV-in-SAV (p = 0.570).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs lifetime management and choice of first prosthesis in younger patients with aortic stenosis.

title: Silent brain infarcts and early cognitive outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 39 studies, 2408 patients (2171 with post-procedural DW-MRI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Largely small observational studies with heterogeneous imaging; meta-regression associations are ecological.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis: silent brain infarcts are common after TAVI, and cerebral embolic protection reduced lesion volume but not incidence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 1601 of 2171 patients had at least one new SBI (pooled effect size 0.76, 95% CI: 0.72-0.81). The incidence of reported stroke with focal neurological deficits was 3%. Early cognitive dysfunction rose from 16% at 10.0 ± 6.3 days to 26% at 6.1 ± 1.7 months.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to the debate on cerebral embolic protection in TAVI.

title: Cerebral Embolic Protection and Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Results From the Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: STS/ACC TVT Registry observational study, 123 186 patients from 599 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data; the instrument assumes site preference affects outcome only through device use.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis found no association between cerebral embolic protection and in-hospital stroke in the primary instrumental variable analysis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In our primary analysis using the instrumental variable model, there was no association between EPD use and in-hospital stroke (adjusted relative risk, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.68-1.13]; absolute risk difference, -0.15% [95% CI, -0.49 to 0.20]). In the propensity score-based model, adjusted odds ratio, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.69-0.97].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large-scale non-randomised evidence on embolic protection during TAVR with discordant estimates by method.

title: Outcomes 2 Years After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients at Low Surgical Risk.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1,000 patients (TAVR vs surgery 1:1); NCT02675114.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; early death and stroke differences attenuated; durability beyond 2 years unknown.
appraisal.one_line: PARTNER 3 at 2 years: TAVR retained a lower primary composite than surgery in low-risk patients, with more valve thrombosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 2-year primary endpoint was 11.5% vs 17.4% (hazard ratio: 0.63; 95% confidence interval: 0.45 to 0.88; p = 0.007). Valve thrombosis was 2.6% vs 0.7% (p = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Mid-term data for TAVI in low-surgical-risk patients, informing guideline age thresholds.

title: Management of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a consensus document of the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI), in collaboration with the ESC Council on Valvular Heart Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus document; prior recommendations were mostly based on expert opinion.
appraisal.one_line: ESC Working Group consensus document updating antithrombotic management during and after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates European guidance on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI in light of recent randomised trials.

title: Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Rheumatic Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Medicare cohort, 1,159 patients with rheumatic AS (SAVR, n = 554; TAVR, n = 605) and 88,554 with nonrheumatic AS undergoing TAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Claims-based identification of rheumatic disease, short follow-up and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare analysis found no mortality difference between TAVR and SAVR in rheumatic aortic stenosis, a population excluded from trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in all-cause mortality with TAVR versus SAVR (11.2 vs. 7.0 per 100 person-year; adjusted hazard ratio: 1.53; 95% confidence interval: 0.84 to 2.79; p = 0.2).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a population excluded from the defining TAVR trials.

title: Valve Academic Research Consortium 3: Updated Endpoint Definitions for Aortic Valve Clinical Research.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from more than 50 experts; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus definitions, not outcome evidence.
appraisal.one_line: VARC-3 consensus updates endpoint definitions for aortic valve clinical research.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standardised endpoints affect comparability of TAVI trials and syntheses.

title: Effect of Denosumab or Alendronic Acid on the Progression of Aortic Stenosis: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised trial; 150 patients (denosumab 49, alendronic acid 51, placebo 50); NCT02132026.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single centre; imaging surrogate rather than clinical endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial: denosumab and alendronic acid did not slow aortic valve calcification in calcific aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Change in aortic valve calcium score at 24 months did not differ between denosumab and placebo (343 [198-804 AU] versus 354 AU [76-675 AU]; P=0.41) or alendronic acid and placebo (326 [138-813 AU] versus 354 AU [76-675 AU]; P=0.49).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Negative result for repurposed drug therapy in aortic stenosis.

title: Impact of Anesthesia Strategy and Valve Type on Clinical Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised 2 x 2 factorial trial; 447 intermediate- to high-risk patients; NCT02737150.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite endpoints and moderate sample size, limited power for components.
appraisal.one_line: SOLVE-TAVI: self-expanding and balloon-expandable valves and general and local anaesthesia gave similar 1-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Valve comparison combined endpoint was 38.3% (BEV) vs 40.4% (SEV) (hazard ratio: 0.94; 95% confidence interval: 0.70 to 1.26; p = 0.66). Anaesthesia comparison combined endpoint was 25.7% vs 23.8% (hazard ratio: 1.09; 95% confidence interval: 0.76 to 1.57; p = 0.63).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised data on two routine TAVI procedural choices.

title: Evaluation and Management of Aortic Stenosis in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Patients with advanced CKD were excluded from randomised trials, so the statement relies on observational evidence.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement on evaluation and management of aortic stenosis in CKD, including surgical versus transcatheter replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses TAVI versus SAVR choice in a population excluded from the defining trials.

title: A randomized evaluation of the TriGuard™ HDH cerebral embolic protection device to Reduce the Impact of Cerebral Embolic LEsions after TransCatheter Aortic Valve ImplanTation: the REFLECT I trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-blind, 2:1 randomised trial; 258 enrolled (54 roll-in, 204 randomised).
appraisal.main_limitation: Underenrolled relative to the planned 375 and used a hierarchical surrogate-heavy endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: REFLECT I: TriGuard cerebral deflection was safe against a performance goal but did not meet the efficacy endpoint in TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary safety outcome met versus performance goal (21.8% vs. 35%, P < 0.0001). Primary hierarchical efficacy endpoint not met (mean efficacy score: -5.3 ± 99.8 TG vs. 11.8 ± 96.4 control, P = 0.31).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to uncertain evidence for cerebral embolic protection in TAVI.

title: Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Patients With Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational matched study; 262 HFrEF patients with moderate AS matched 1:1 with 262 without AS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, confounded by indication, with only 44 patients undergoing AVR.
appraisal.one_line: Matched series: moderate aortic stenosis in HFrEF carried higher mortality, with TAVR associated with improved survival.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Moderate AS was associated with increased mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.98; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.08 to 4.31). AVR was associated with improved survival (HR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.35 to 0.98; p = 0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a randomised trial of early TAVI in moderate AS with HFrEF.

title: Eight-year outcomes for patients with aortic valve stenosis at low surgical risk randomized to transcatheter vs. surgical aortic valve replacement.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 280 patients (TAVI n = 145, SAVR n = 135); mean age 79.1 ± 4.8 years, mean STS score 3.0 ± 1.7%.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial, so event comparisons are imprecise; the abstract gives P values rather than hazard ratios.
appraisal.one_line: Eight-year follow-up of the NOTION trial found similar clinical outcomes after TAVI and SAVR in low-risk patients, with less structural valve deterioration after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 8 years the estimated risk of all-cause mortality, stroke or myocardial infarction was 54.5% after TAVI and 54.8% after SAVR (P = 0.94). Structural valve deterioration was 13.9% vs. 28.3% (P = 0.0017); bioprosthetic valve failure was 8.7% vs. 10.5% (P = 0.61).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised durability data for TAVI in low-risk patients, relevant to the choice of TAVI or SAVR in younger patients.

title: Edoxaban versus Vitamin K Antagonist for Atrial Fibrillation after TAVR.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label, adjudicator-masked trial, 1426 patients (713 per group), mean age 82.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, and noninferiority for major bleeding was not shown.
appraisal.one_line: ENVISAGE-TAVI AF found edoxaban noninferior to vitamin K antagonists for a composite of adverse events after TAVR, with more major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite primary efficacy outcome was 17.3 per 100 person-years with edoxaban and 16.5 with vitamin K antagonists (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.85 to 1.31; P = 0.01 for noninferiority). Major bleeding was 9.7 vs. 7.0 per 100 person-years (hazard ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.91; P = 0.93 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs oral anticoagulant choice in patients with atrial fibrillation after TAVR, with a safety signal for gastrointestinal bleeding.

title: Association Between Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Bicuspid vs Tricuspid Aortic Stenosis and Mortality or Stroke Among Patients at Low Surgical Risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 37 660 low-risk patients (3243 bicuspid, 34 417 tricuspid); 3168 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with potential selection bias and no surgically treated bicuspid comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of low-risk TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve found similar early and 1-year mortality and stroke in bicuspid and tricuspid stenosis.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large dataset on bicuspid TAVR in low-risk patients, a group excluded from the pivotal trials.

title: Comparison of a Pure Plug-Based Versus a Primary Suture-Based Vascular Closure Device Strategy for Transfemoral Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: The CHOICE-CLOSURE Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial, 516 patients (258 per group), mean age 80.5±6.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Index-hospitalisation endpoint only and a modest sample size.
appraisal.one_line: CHOICE-CLOSURE found more access-related complications with a plug-based than a suture-based closure strategy after transfemoral TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 19.4% (50/258) of the pure plug-based group and 12.0% (31/258) of the primary suture-based group (relative risk, 1.61 [95% CI, 1.07-2.44], P=0.029).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised device comparison for a routine TAVR step, favouring the suture-based strategy for complications.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement Versus Conservative Treatment in Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: The AVATAR Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised event-driven trial, 157 patients (78 early surgery, 79 conservative) at 9 European centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with few events, and surgery rather than TAVI was the intervention.
appraisal.one_line: AVATAR found that early surgery reduced a composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke or heart failure hospitalisation in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There were 39 events, 13 in early surgery and 26 in conservative treatment (hazard ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.23-0.90]; P=0.02). Secondary endpoints including all-cause mortality did not differ statistically.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the case for early intervention in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis, a key timing question for TAVI.

title: Edoxaban Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Leaflet Thrombosis and Cerebral Thromboembolism After TAVR: The ADAPT-TAVR Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 229 patients in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered, as the authors state, with imaging endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: ADAPT-TAVR found numerically lower leaflet thrombosis with edoxaban than DAPT after TAVR, but the difference was not significant.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Leaflet thrombosis was 9.8% vs 18.4% (absolute difference, -8.5% [95% CI, -17.8% to 0.8%]; P=0.076). New cerebral lesions were 25.0% vs 20.2% (difference, 4.8%; 95% CI, -6.4% to 16.0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic therapy after TAVR in patients without an anticoagulation indication.

title: Effect of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement on All-Cause Mortality in Patients With Aortic Stenosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised noninferiority trial at 34 UK centres; 913 patients (458 TAVI, 455 surgery).
appraisal.main_limitation: Moderate-risk population with mixed valve types and access routes; 1-year follow-up only, with more pacemaker implantation and vascular complications after TAVI.
appraisal.one_line: UK randomised trial found TAVI noninferior to surgical replacement for 1-year all-cause mortality in patients aged 70 or older at moderately increased operative risk.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, there were 21 deaths (4.6%) in the TAVI group and 30 deaths (6.6%) in the surgery group, with an adjusted absolute risk difference of -2.0% (1-sided 97.5% CI, -∞ to 1.2%; P < .001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pragmatic randomised evidence in a large mortality-defined population that informs TAVI versus SAVR decisions and guideline recommendations.

title: Apixaban vs. standard of care after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the ATLANTIS trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised open-label superiority trial; 1500 patients (749 apixaban, 751 standard of care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a broad composite; stratum analyses were exploratory, and a higher non-cardiovascular mortality signal was observed with apixaban.
appraisal.one_line: ATLANTIS randomised 1500 patients after TAVI to apixaban or standard of care; apixaban was not superior on the composite primary endpoint.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 138 (18.4%) and 151 (20.1%) patients receiving apixaban or standard of care, respectively [hazard ratio (HR) 0.92; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.73-1.16]; the primary safety endpoint was similar (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.72-1.44).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised evidence on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI that bears directly on guideline recommendations for anticoagulation versus antiplatelet therapy.

title: Balloon- vs Self-Expanding Valve Systems for Failed Small Surgical Aortic Valve Bioprostheses.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 102 patients randomised, 98 underwent ViV-TAVR (BEV: n = 46, SEV: n = 52).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with a haemodynamic primary endpoint at 30 days and no clinical outcome follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of balloon-expandable and self-expanding valves for valve-in-valve TAVR in small failed surgical bioprostheses favoured the self-expanding valve on echocardiographic gradients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients in the SEV group exhibited lower mean and maximal transvalvular gradient values (15 ± 8 mm Hg vs 23 ± 8 mm Hg; P ˂ 0.001; 28 ± 16 mm Hg vs 40 ± 13 mm Hg, P ˂ 0.001); there were no deaths or strokes at 30 days.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Valve choice for small failed bioprostheses is a recurrent decision, and this is the first randomised haemodynamic comparison.

title: Cerebral Embolic Protection during Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial across North America, Europe and Australia; 3000 patients (1501 CEP, 1499 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Confidence interval does not exclude a benefit, and the trial was industry-funded.
appraisal.one_line: PROTECTED TAVR randomised 3000 patients to transfemoral TAVR with or without cerebral embolic protection; periprocedural stroke did not differ significantly.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of stroke within 72 hours after TAVR or before discharge did not differ significantly between the CEP group and the control group (2.3% vs. 2.9%; difference, -0.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -1.7 to 0.5; P = 0.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest randomised test of cerebral embolic protection in TAVR (D3), directly relevant to routine device use.

title: ESC/EACTS vs. ACC/AHA guidelines for the management of severe aortic stenosis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline comparison review; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Narrative comparison, not a systematic evidence appraisal, covering guidelines that predate the latest trials.
appraisal.one_line: State of the art review compares the 2021 ESC/EACTS and 2020 ACC/AHA aortic stenosis guidelines and identifies three areas of divergence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents ESC versus ACC/AHA discordance on timing of intervention, valve choice and TAVI versus SAVR age thresholds (D3).

title: Transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in lower-risk and higher-risk patients: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; eight RCTs with 8698 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with a pragmatic risk classification and heterogeneous valve platforms and follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of eight randomised trials found early mortality was lower after TAVI than SAVR in lower-risk patients but not after 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In lower-risk patients, at 1 year, the risk of death was lower after TAVI compared with SAVR [relative risk (RR) 0.67; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.47 to 0.96, P = 0.031], as was death or disabling stroke (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.50 to 0.92, P = 0.014).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Frames TAVI versus SAVR in lower-risk patients (D3), where long-term durability data remain pending.

title: 3-Year Outcomes After Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients With Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1,414 attempted implantations (730 TAVR; 684 surgery), mean age 74 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary difference did not reach conventional significance, and pacemaker rates were higher with TAVR.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year outcomes of TAVR versus surgery in low-risk aortic stenosis from the Evolut Low Risk study.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the primary endpoint occurred in 7.4% of TAVR patients and 10.4% of surgery patients (HR: 0.70; 95% CI: 0.49-1.00; P = 0.051).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the durability and choice of TAVR in younger low-risk patients.

title: Effect of Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch on Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational nationwide cohort from SWEDEHEART and other national registers, 16,423 patients (no PPM: 7,377; moderate PPM: 8,502; severe PPM: 544).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with residual confounding; PPM was associated with outcomes but causality cannot be inferred.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide Swedish cohort relating prosthesis-patient mismatch after bioprosthetic SAVR to long-term mortality and heart failure hospitalisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After regression standardization, 10-year all-cause mortality was 43% (95% CI: 24%-44%) with no PPM, 45% (95% CI: 43%-46%) with moderate PPM and 48% (95% CI: 44%-51%) with severe PPM. The survival difference at 10 years was 4.6% (95% CI: 0.7%-8.5%) for no vs severe PPM and 1.7% (95% CI: 0.1%-3.3%) for no vs moderate PPM. The difference in heart failure hospitalization at 10 years was 6.0% (95% CI: 2.2%-9.7%) for severe vs no PPM.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the long-term cost of mismatch, informing valve sizing and the choice of strategy in younger patients with bioprosthetic SAVR.

title: Economic Outcomes of Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients with Severe Aortic Stenosis and Low Surgical Risk: Results from the PARTNER 3 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Economic substudy of the randomised PARTNER 3 trial, 929 of 1000 low-risk patients included, with lifetime Markov model from the US health care perspective.
appraisal.main_limitation: Long-term conclusions depend on extrapolated survival and US costs; results were sensitive to a modest late survival advantage with SAVR.
appraisal.one_line: Cost-effectiveness analysis of transfemoral TAVR versus SAVR in low-risk patients from the PARTNER 3 trial using a Markov model.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR led to 2-year cost savings of $2030/patient compared with SAVR (95% CI, -$6222 to $1816) and a gain of 0.05 quality-adjusted life-years (95% CI, -0.003 to 0.102). TAVR was projected to be economically dominant, with a 95% probability that the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio would be <$50 000/quality-adjusted life-year gained.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs payer and guideline decisions on TAVR in low-risk patients while long-term durability remains unsettled.

title: Outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with cardiogenic shock.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 309 505 TAVR patients, of whom 5006 (1.6%) presented with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with heterogeneous shock definitions and no comparison to alternative treatments such as balloon valvuloplasty or medical therapy.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC TVT registry analysis of balloon-expandable TAVR in patients presenting with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In propensity-matched analysis, cardiogenic shock was associated with higher in-hospital (9.9% vs. 2.7%), 30-day (12.9% vs. 4.9%) and 1-year (29.7% vs. 22.6%) mortality. In the landmark analysis after 30 days, 1-year mortality was similar (hazard ratio [HR] 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.95-1.21).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides outcome estimates in a population excluded from pivotal trials and informs the shock-TAVR decision.

title: Outcomes of SAPIEN 3 Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Compared With Surgical Valve Replacement in Intermediate-Risk Patients.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Propensity-matched analysis of trial cohorts; 783 matched pairs of intermediate-risk patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised matched comparison across separate trial cohorts.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year propensity-matched comparison of SAPIEN 3 TAVR and surgery in intermediate-risk aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There were no differences in the primary endpoint between S3 TAVR and SAVR at 5 years (40.2% vs 42.7%; HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.74-1.03; P = 0.10).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds mid-term outcomes and durability data for TAVR in intermediate-risk patients.

title: Effectiveness of aortic valve replacement in Heyde syndrome: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 33 studies (32 observational studies and one randomized controlled trial) on acquired von Willebrand syndrome (n = 1054) and 11 observational studies on gastrointestinal bleeding (n = 300).
appraisal.main_limitation: Almost entirely observational studies without control groups.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of aortic valve replacement outcomes in Heyde syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The pooled proportion of Heyde patients with acquired von Willebrand syndrome recovery was 86% (95% CI, 79%-91%) at T1, and gastrointestinal bleeding cessation was 73% (62%-81%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports valve replacement in Heyde syndrome with aortic stenosis.

title: Outcomes of repeat transcatheter aortic valve replacement with balloon-expandable valves: a registry study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry study of 350 591 patients (1320 redo-TAVR; 349 271 native-TAVR), 1320 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry limited to balloon-expandable valves with short follow-up, in a setting funded by the manufacturer.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC registry comparison of redo-TAVR with balloon-expandable valves versus native-valve TAVR using propensity matching.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant difference between redo-TAVR and native-TAVR in death at 30 days (4·7% vs 4·0%, p=0·36) or 1 year (17·5% vs 19·0%, p=0·57), and stroke at 30 days (2·0% vs 1·9%, p=0·84) or 1 year (3·2% vs 3·5%, p=0·80). Coronary compression or obstruction occurred in four [0·3%] of 1320.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs lifetime management planning in younger TAVR candidates, where durability and redo feasibility drive valve choice.

title: Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients at Five Years.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1000 patients, 503 assigned to TAVR and 497 to surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Some patients are missing from the first primary end point analysis and the primary comparison was not significant.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year results of TAVR versus surgery in low-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier estimates for the first primary end point were 22.8% in the TAVR group and 27.2% in the surgery group (difference, -4.3 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -9.9 to 1.3; P = 0.07).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides durability data on TAVR in low-risk patients.

title: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 349 patients enrolled (177 TAVR + LAAO and 172 TAVR + medical therapy) at 34 US centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority design with limited sample size and added procedural complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of concomitant LAAO with TAVR versus TAVR with medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For the composite primary end point, TAVR + LAAO was noninferior to TAVR + medical therapy (22.7 versus 27.3 events per 100 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.60-1.22]; Pnoninferiority<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic strategy and device combination in TAVR patients with AF.

title: The Mortality Burden of Untreated Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of 1,669,536 echocardiographic reports (1,085,850 patients) from 24 U.S. hospitals, 595,120 patients with available AS severity.
appraisal.main_limitation: Echocardiographic report data with possible misclassification of severity and confounding by comorbidity.
appraisal.one_line: Large US real-world dataset describing untreated mortality and treatment rates across the full spectrum of aortic stenosis severity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: KM-estimated 4-year unadjusted, untreated, all-cause mortality was 13.5% (95% CI: 13.3%-13.7%) with no AS, 33.5% (95% CI: 31.0%-35.8%) for moderate, and 44.9% (95% CI: 39.9%-49.6%) for severe AS. KM-estimated 4-year observed treatment rates were 60.7% (95% CI: 58.0%-63.3%) for severe AS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the case for trials of earlier intervention in moderate and asymptomatic AS.

title: Treatment of severe symptomatic aortic valve stenosis using non-invasive ultrasound therapy: a cohort study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicentre, single-arm series of 40 adult patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, 6-month data (NCT03779620, NCT04665596).
appraisal.main_limitation: Uncontrolled, small and short follow-up, with modest haemodynamic change and device-maker funding.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm study of non-invasive transthoracic ultrasound therapy to soften calcified aortic valves in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Procedure-related mortality did not occur. Mean aortic valve area rose from 0·58 cm2 (SD 0·19) at baseline to 0·64 cm2 (0·21) at follow-up (p=0·0088), and mean pressure gradient fell from 41·9 mm Hg (20·1) to 38·8 mm Hg (17·8; p=0·024).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A novel non-interventional route for patients unsuitable for valve replacement, requiring controlled evaluation.

title: Transcatheter or surgical aortic valve implantation: 10-year outcomes of the NOTION trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 280 patients randomised to TAVI with the self-expanding CoreValve (n = 145) or SAVR (n = 135).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial of one self-expanding valve in a mostly lower-risk population, with long-term attrition and few structural events.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of the NOTION trial shows no difference in major clinical outcomes between TAVI and SAVR, with less severe structural valve deterioration after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of the composite outcome all-cause mortality, stroke, or myocardial infarction was 65.5% after TAVI and 65.5% after SAVR [hazard ratio (HR) 1.0; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.7-1.3; P = .9]. Severe SVD had occurred in 1.5% and 10.0% (HR 0.2; 95% CI 0.04-0.7; P = .02) after TAVI and SAVR, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the longest randomised durability data comparing TAVI with SAVR in lower-risk patients.

title: Reducing length of stay after transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the FAST-TAVI II trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 969 patients in the intervention group and 860 patients in the control group, cluster randomised, multicentre.
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up and a process endpoint, with a small absolute difference in median length of stay.
appraisal.one_line: Cluster-randomised FAST-TAVI II trial shows a structured care programme increased early discharge after transfemoral TAVI without a difference in 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early discharge was achieved in 563 (58.1%) patients in the intervention group vs. 364 (42.3%) patients in the control group (P < .0001). Thirty-day mortality was low and similar in the two groups (0.5% vs. 0.9%, P = .30), as were 30-day readmissions (4.6% vs. 2.8%, P = .28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports systematic early discharge pathways after TAVI, a systems question with resource consequences.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation in patients with high-risk symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (ALIGN-AR): a prospective, multicentre, single-arm study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicentre, single-arm study at 20 US sites, 180 patients enrolled (NCT04415047).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design against performance goals, no surgical comparator and manufacturer funding.
appraisal.one_line: ALIGN-AR single-arm trial of the Trilogy transcatheter valve for high-risk native aortic regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Technical success was achieved in 171 (95%) patients. The primary safety endpoint was achieved, with events occurring in 48 (27% [97·5% CI 19·2-34·0]) patients (pnon-inferiority<0·0001). The primary efficacy endpoint was achieved, with mortality in 14 (7·8% [3·3-12·3]) patients at 1 year (pnon-inferiority<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First dedicated-device evidence for TAVI in pure aortic regurgitation, a population without a guideline-endorsed transcatheter option.

title: Self-Expanding or Balloon-Expandable TAVR in Patients with a Small Aortic Annulus.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 716 patients treated at 83 sites in 13 countries (mean age, 80 years; 87% women).
appraisal.main_limitation: Twelve-month follow-up with a hemodynamic composite as the superiority endpoint, and the trial was industry funded.
appraisal.one_line: SMART showed a self-expanding supra-annular TAVR valve was noninferior on clinical outcomes and superior on bioprosthetic valve dysfunction at 12 months in small annuli.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died, had a disabling stroke, or were rehospitalized for heart failure through 12 months was 9.4% with the self-expanding valve and 10.6% with the balloon-expandable valve (difference, -1.2 percentage points; 90% confidence interval [CI], -4.9 to 2.5; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs valve selection in women and small annuli, where valve haemodynamics may affect long-term durability.

title: Transcatheter or Surgical Treatment of Aortic-Valve Stenosis.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 1414 patients randomised (701 to TAVI, 713 to SAVR) at 38 German sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: One-year follow-up only, with durability in younger low-risk patients unaddressed.
appraisal.one_line: DEDICATE found TAVI noninferior to SAVR for death or stroke at 1 year in low- and intermediate-risk patients in routine practice.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary outcome at 1 year was 5.4% in the TAVI group and 10.0% in the SAVR group (hazard ratio for death or stroke, 0.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.35 to 0.79; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large pragmatic trial that supports TAVI in low-risk patients and bears on ESC and ACC/AHA age thresholds.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation in low-risk tricuspid or bicuspid aortic stenosis: the NOTION-2 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 370 low-risk patients aged 75 years or under randomised 1:1 to TAVI or surgery; 100 patients had bicuspid AS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide confidence intervals, one-year follow-up and a small bicuspid subgroup with a non-significant interaction.
appraisal.one_line: NOTION-2 found a similar one-year composite with TAVI and surgery in low-risk patients aged 75 or under, with a signal of worse outcomes in bicuspid stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year incidence of the primary endpoint was 10.2% in the TAVI group and 7.1% in the surgery group [absolute risk difference 3.1%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -2.7% to 8.8%; hazard ratio (HR) 1.4; 95% CI, 0.7-2.9; P = .3].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs TAVI use in younger low-risk and bicuspid patients, where durability and outcomes remain uncertain.

title: Leaflet modification before transcatheter aortic valve implantation in patients at risk for coronary obstruction: the ShortCut study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-arm pivotal study, Sixty eligible patients treated at 22 clinical sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small single-arm study with 30- to 90-day follow-up and no comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Pivotal ShortCut study of a dedicated leaflet-splitting device before TAVI in patients at risk of coronary obstruction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Successful leaflet splitting was achieved in all [100%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 94%-100.0%, P < .001] patients. Freedom from the primary safety endpoint was achieved in 59 [98.3%; 95% CI (91.1%-100%)] patients, with no mortality and one (1.7%) disabling stroke.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device evidence for managing coronary obstruction risk in valve-in-valve TAVI.

title: LANDMARK comparison of early outcomes of newer-generation Myval transcatheter heart valve series with contemporary valves (Sapien and Evolut) in real-world individuals with severe symptomatic native aortic stenosis: a randomised non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 768 participants randomly assigned (384 to Myval, 384 to a contemporary THV) at 31 hospitals in 16 countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Thirty-day composite endpoint with a wide non-inferiority margin of 10·44%, open-label, and funded by the manufacturer.
appraisal.one_line: LANDMARK found the Myval balloon-expandable valve noninferior to contemporary Sapien or Evolut valves for a 30-day composite.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint showed non-inferiority of the Myval (25%) compared with contemporary THV (27%), with a risk difference of -2·3% (one-sided upper 95% CI 3·8, pnon-inferiority<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides randomised evidence for a newer valve platform, though durability is unaddressed.

title: Contemporary Outcomes and Trends for the Transseptal Mitral Valve-in-Valve Procedure Using Balloon Expandable Transcatheter Valves in the United States.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 4243 patients with a mean±SD STS score of 9.2±7.7 at 455 sites, 2015 to September 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a surgical comparator.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC registry analysis of contemporary transseptal mitral valve-in-valve with balloon-expandable valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause in-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year mortality rates were 3.2%, 4.3%, and 13.4%, respectively. NYHA class I/II rose from 18% to 87% and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score from 38 to 78 at 1 year (P<0.0001 for both).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contemporary benchmarks for transseptal MViV supporting its use in degenerated bioprostheses.

title: Clinical Significance of Diffusion-Weighted Brain MRI Lesions After TAVR: Results of a Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level data pooled from 4 prospective TAVR embolic protection studies, 495 of 603 patients completing predischarge DW-MRI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled study cohorts with a surrogate imaging measure; incomplete MRI in some patients.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis relating DW-MRI lesion burden after TAVR to clinical stroke.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The C-statistic was 0.84 for TLV, 0.81 for number of lesions, and 0.82 for maximum ILV in predicting ischemic stroke. Patients with a TLV >500 mm3 (vs TLV ≤500 mm3) had more ischemic stroke (18.2% vs 2.3%; P < 0.0001) and more disabling strokes (8.8% vs 0.9%; P < 0.0001) at 30 days.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports DW-MRI lesion volume as a surrogate in cerebral protection trials.

title: PCI in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 455 patients randomised (227 PCI, 228 conservative treatment), median follow-up 2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial of modest size with a confidence interval near unity and the composite driven partly by revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: NOTION-3 found PCI of significant coronary stenoses in patients undergoing TAVI reduced a composite of death, MI or urgent revascularisation, at the cost of more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A major adverse cardiac event (primary end point) had occurred in 60 patients (26%) in the PCI group and in 81 (36%) in the conservative-treatment group (hazard ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51 to 0.99; P = 0.04). A bleeding event occurred in 64 patients (28%) in the PCI group and in 45 (20%) in the conservative-treatment group (hazard ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.03 to 2.22).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives the first randomised evidence on managing coronary disease in TAVI candidates, a common clinical decision.

title: Continuation versus Interruption of Oral Anticoagulation during TAVI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 858 patients in the modified intention-to-treat population (431 continuation, 427 interruption).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial with a 30-day horizon and a wide confidence interval, so thromboembolic risk of interruption is imprecisely estimated.
appraisal.one_line: POPular PAUSE TAVI found that continuing oral anticoagulation during TAVI was not noninferior to interruption and increased bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 71 patients (16.5%) in the continuation group and in 63 (14.8%) in the interruption group (risk difference, 1.7 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.6; P = 0.18 for noninferiority). Bleeding occurred in 134 patients (31.1%) in the continuation group and in 91 (21.3%) in the interruption group (risk difference, 9.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 3.9 to 15.6).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs periprocedural anticoagulation practice for the third of TAVI patients taking oral anticoagulants.

title: Aortic valve replacement vs. conservative treatment in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis: long-term follow-up of the AVATAR trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 157 low-risk patients randomised (78 early AVR, 79 conservative), median follow-up 63 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, open-label trial with surgical rather than transcatheter intervention.
appraisal.one_line: Extended AVATAR follow-up reports lower composite events with early surgical AVR than watchful waiting in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite endpoint outcome event occurred in 18/78 patients (23.1%) in the early surgery group and in 37/79 patients (46.8%) in the conservative treatment group [hazard ratio (HR) early surgery vs. conservative treatment 0.42; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.24-0.73, P = .002].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to trial evidence on early intervention in asymptomatic aortic stenosis, a guideline-contested decision.

title: Early Intervention in Patients With Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis and Myocardial Fibrosis: The EVOLVED Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized open-label trial; 224 eligible patients of the originally planned sample size of 356.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped short of planned enrolment, so the trial is underpowered and the confidence interval is wide.
appraisal.one_line: EVOLVED did not show a significant benefit of early valve intervention in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis with myocardial fibrosis, but was underpowered.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 20 of 113 patients (18%) in the early intervention group and 25 of 111 patients (23%) in the guideline-directed conservative management group (hazard ratio, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.44-1.43]; P = .44).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence on timing of intervention in asymptomatic aortic stenosis alongside other recent randomized trials.

title: Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement for Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial at 75 centers; 901 patients (455 TAVR, 446 clinical surveillance).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with the benefit driven mainly by unplanned cardiovascular hospitalization and with 87.0% of the surveillance group eventually undergoing valve replacement.
appraisal.one_line: EARLY TAVR randomized trial found early TAVR superior to clinical surveillance in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 122 patients (26.8%) in the TAVR group and in 202 patients (45.3%) in the clinical surveillance group (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.40 to 0.63; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly challenges the guideline recommendation of routine surveillance in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Systolic Heart Failure and Moderate Aortic Stenosis: TAVR UNLOAD.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized controlled trial; 178 patients (TAVR n = 89, surveillance n = 89).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size, and 43% of the surveillance group crossed over to TAVR.
appraisal.one_line: TAVR UNLOAD did not show superiority of TAVR over surveillance for moderate aortic stenosis with HFrEF, though quality of life improved.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR was associated with wins in 47.6% of pairs, compared with 36.6% in the CASS group, resulting in a win ratio of 1.31 (95% CI: 0.91-1.88; P = 0.14).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses intervention in moderate aortic stenosis, an area without randomized evidence of hard outcome benefit.

title: Definitions of clinical study outcome measures for cardiovascular diseases: the European Unified Registries for Heart Care Evaluation and Randomized Trials (EuroHeart).

appraisal.design_and_n: Modified Delphi consensus informed by systematic review, drawing on a consortium of 82 experts across five working groups.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus definitions depend on expert agreement and have not yet been tested for uptake across trials and registries.
appraisal.one_line: ESC EuroHeart international data standards defining outcome measures for ACS/PCI, AF, HF and TAVI studies.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 24 Level 1 (generic: 5, ACS/PCI: 8, AF: 2; HF: 5, TAVI: 4) and 48 Level 2 (generic: 18, ACS-PCI: 7, AF: 6, HF: 2, TAVI: 15) outcome measures were defined.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Harmonised outcome definitions would improve comparability of registries and trials and ease pooling in future syntheses.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement vs Clinical Surveillance in Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 4 RCTs; 1,427 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with substantial heterogeneity for mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four trials found early AVR reduced unplanned hospitalisation and stroke but not mortality in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early AVR was associated with a significant reduction in unplanned cardiovascular or HF hospitalization (pooled rate 14.6% vs 31.9%; HR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.30-0.53) and stroke (HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.40-0.97). All-cause mortality HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.40-1.17.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Synthesises the randomized evidence for early intervention in asymptomatic aortic stenosis.

title: TransCatheter aortic valve implantation and fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus conventional surgical aortic valve replacement and coronary bypass grafting for treatment of patients with aortic valve stenosis and complex or multivessel coronary disease (TCW): an international, multicentre, prospective, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label multicentre randomized non-inferiority trial; 172 patients (91 PCI plus TAVI, 81 SAVR plus CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial that stopped enrolment below a large sample and evaluated 77 patients in the surgical group.
appraisal.one_line: TCW found FFR-guided PCI plus TAVI favourable versus SAVR plus CABG in severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint four [4%] of 91 patients versus 17 [23%] of 77 patients; risk difference -18·5 [90% CI -27·8 to -9·7]; hazard ratio 0·17 [95% CI 0·06-0·51].
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomized comparison for combined aortic stenosis and complex coronary disease.

title: Predictors of Outcomes of Reintervention After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: FRANCE 2 and FRANCE TAVI Registries.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 72,850 patients from FRANCE 2 and FRANCE TAVI, 2010 to 2022, with competing-risk analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up is too short to define reintervention risk in younger low-risk patients, and indications for reintervention were not adjudicated.
appraisal.one_line: French national registries quantify the incidence and predictors of reintervention after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The cumulative incidence of overall reintervention at 8 years was 1.7% including 591 patients who had redo TAVR and 111 patients who required explant TAVR. Six-year mortality was high but was similar in patients who had early and late reintervention (76.2% vs 64.0%; P = 0.77).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives denominator-based reintervention rates relevant to lifetime management planning as TAVR extends to younger patients.

title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Lower-Risk Patients: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomized trials with reconstructed time-to-event IPD; Six trials enrolling 5,341 lower-risk patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Most patients lacked 5-year follow-up and pooled mortality may change with longer data.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of six lower-risk TAVR versus SAVR trials associated TAVR with lower 5-year mortality using reconstructed IPD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR was associated with a 20% reduction in the hazard of all-cause death (HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.66-0.97; P = 0.02) and stroke HR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.74-1.26.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes to the lower-risk TAVR versus SAVR debate and to heart team decisions.

title: 5-Year Outcomes After Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients With Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial; 1,414 patients underwent an attempted implant (n = 730 TAVR, n = 684 surgery).
appraisal.main_limitation: Low-risk population with a mean age of 74 years, so lifetime durability remains unanswered.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year randomized results in low-risk patients show comparable all-cause mortality or disabling stroke after TAVR or surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years the Kaplan-Meier estimate for the primary endpoint of all-cause mortality or disabling stroke was 15.5% for the TAVR group and 16.4% for the surgery group (P = 0.47).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports TAVR as an alternative in low-risk patients with mid-term outcomes.

title: Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized open-label controlled trial in Spain; 1222 patients in the primary analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, driven by heart failure worsening rather than mortality, with exclusions after randomization.
appraisal.one_line: DapaTAVI found dapagliflozin lowered death from any cause or worsening heart failure in high-risk patients undergoing TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 91 patients (15.0%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 124 patients (20.1%) in the standard-care group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.95; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Introduces a post-TAVI drug therapy that could change practice for patients at high risk of heart failure events.

title: Routine Cerebral Embolic Protection during Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized controlled trial across 33 centers; 7635 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: United Kingdom centres with one device type.
appraisal.one_line: BHF PROTECT-TAVI found routine cerebral embolic protection did not reduce stroke within 72 hours of TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 81 of 3795 participants (2.1%) in the CEP group and in 82 of 3799 participants (2.2%) in the control group (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -0.68 to 0.63; P = 0.94).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest trial of cerebral embolic protection, informing guideline positions on routine use.

title: Transcatheter vs. surgical aortic valve replacement in women: the RHEIA trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial in 48 European centres; 443 women randomized, 420 treated as randomized.
appraisal.main_limitation: One-year follow-up, with the composite driven by rehospitalisation.
appraisal.one_line: RHEIA found TAVI superior to surgery for a composite of death, stroke or rehospitalisation at 1 year in women with severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier estimates of the primary endpoint event rates at 1 year were 8.9% in the TAVI and 15.6% in the surgery group. This difference of -6.8% with an upper 95% confidence limit of -1.5% demonstrated the non-inferiority of TAVI (P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides sex-specific randomized evidence for TAVI versus surgery.

title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients in the United States: A Report From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry cohort of 383 030 TAVR patients; 108 407 (28%) designated low-risk by the heart team, 42 093 trial-eligible.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry data without a comparator and with short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: STS/ACC TVT registry describes real-world outcomes of low-risk TAVR against pivotal trial populations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the overall heart team-designated low-risk population, 30-day outcomes included 0.8% mortality, 1.5% stroke, and 8.4% new permanent pacemaker requirement; 1-year outcomes included 4.6% mortality, 2.6% stroke, and 90% alive and well.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Benchmarks low-risk TAVR outcomes in routine US practice and shows event rates higher than in trials.

title: ACURATE neo2 valve versus commercially available transcatheter heart valves in patients with severe aortic stenosis (ACURATE IDE): a multicentre, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised non-inferiority trial at 71 centres; ACURATE neo2 752 patients, control 748 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single device comparison funded by the manufacturer, with a primary composite driven by multiple components.
appraisal.one_line: ACURATE IDE did not meet non-inferiority for ACURATE neo2 versus commercial valves, with worse outcomes at 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, all-cause mortality occurred in 36 of 752 patients in the ACURATE neo2 group versus 28 of 748 patients in the control group (HR 1·30 [95% CI 0·80-2·14]), stroke in 41 patients versus 25 patients (1·68 [1·02-2·75]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on valve-specific performance and safety in TAVR.

title: Cardiac transthyretin amyloidosis treatment improves outcomes after aortic valve replacement for severe stenosis.

appraisal.design_and_n: International registry of 226 patients with dual pathology from 16 centres in 10 countries, compared with a matched lone AS control cohort.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised with treatment selection and immortal time concerns in a small population.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry associates ATTR-specific medication and AVR with survival in patients with dual aortic stenosis and ATTR amyloidosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: ATTR-specific medication was independently associated with lower all-cause (weighted hazard ratio (HR) 0.40, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.24-0.68) and CV mortality (weighted HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27-0.83) but not HHF. AVR improved survival in the overall (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93) and severe AS cohort (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.26-0.70).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports treating both conditions in dual AS-amyloid disease, a growing TAVR population.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Balloon- Versus Self-Expandable Bioprostheses for the Treatment of Bicuspid Aortic Valve Stenosis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry of 1443 consecutive patients at 29 centres, BE-THV (n=860) and SE-THV (n=583).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised with device choice driven by anatomy and operator preference.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre propensity-matched comparison of balloon- versus self-expandable valves for bicuspid TAVR to 3 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In-hospital and 30-day death or stroke did not significantly differ between BE-THV and SE-THV groups (5.1% versus 6.1%; hazard ratio after propensity score matching, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.51-2.02]). At 3 years, death or stroke was not significantly different (23.7% versus 26.2%; hazard ratio after propensity score matching, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.65-1.51]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs valve selection in bicuspid anatomy, an area largely excluded from pivotal trials.

title: Peri-Interventional Anesthesia Strategies for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label noninferiority RCT, 752 patients (MA 377, SoC 375) at 10 German sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with higher patient-reported anxiety and stress in the minimalist arm and a wide two-sided interval.
appraisal.one_line: DOUBLE-CHOICE randomised trial found a minimalist transfemoral TAVI approach with local anaesthesia noninferior to conscious sedation for a 30-day composite.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 80 (22.9%) of 350 patients in the MA group and in 91 (25.8%) of 353 patients in the SoC group (rate difference, 2.9%; lower boundary of the 1-sided 95% CI, -2.4%; P for noninferiority=0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides randomised support for local anaesthesia as the default in routine transfemoral TAVI.

title: Three-Year Follow-Up of the NOTION-2 Trial: TAVR Versus SAVR to Treat Younger Low-Risk Patients With Tricuspid or Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 370 patients (mean age, 71.1 years) randomised 1:1 to TAVR or surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with wide intervals in the bicuspid subgroup (hazard ratio, 2.9; 95% CI, 0.9-9.0).
appraisal.one_line: Three-year NOTION-2 results show similar outcomes with TAVR and surgery in low-risk patients aged 60 to 75 years, with a non-significant signal against TAVR in bicuspid anatomy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the primary composite end point occurred in 16.1% of patients with TAVR versus 12.6% in surgical patients (hazard ratio, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.8-2.2%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice of TAVR versus surgery in younger low-risk patients and the contested question of bicuspid valves.

title: Impact of Cerebral Embolic Protection on Cognitive Function After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Data From the BHF PROTECT-TAVI Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial, 3535 participants (SENTINEL CEP 1763, control 1772).
appraisal.main_limitation: Restricted to participants who underwent telephone cognitive assessment, and a secondary rather than primary trial analysis.
appraisal.one_line: Secondary analysis of BHF PROTECT-TAVI found no effect of cerebral embolic protection on cognitive change after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in means between the treatment groups (-0.07 [95% CI, -0.22 to 0.09], P=0.42) for change in total t-MoCA score.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence that routine cerebral embolic protection offers no cognitive benefit in TAVI.

title: Sex-specific outcomes after transcatheter or surgical treatment of aortic valve stenosis: the DEDICATE-DZHK6 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Predefined descriptive subgroup analysis of a randomised trial, 1394 patients (43.3% women).
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive subgroup analysis without formal interaction testing reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Predefined sex subgroup of DEDICATE-DZHK6 shows lower one-year death or stroke with TAVI than SAVR in both women and men, with a stroke difference in women.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause death or stroke at 1 year was 5.2% in the TAVI vs 11.5% in the SAVR group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.46; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.25-0.82] in women and 5.4% vs 9.0% (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.35-1.03) in men.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds sex-specific randomised evidence to the TAVI versus SAVR decision in low- to intermediate-risk patients.

title: Left Ventricular Health and TAVR Timing in Asymptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis: Analysis From the EARLY TAVR Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial, 901 patients (TAVR 455, clinical surveillance 446) at 75 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Effect-modification analyses by LV health were exploratory because it was not prespecified as a stratification variable.
appraisal.one_line: EARLY TAVR analysis found the benefit of early TAVR over clinical surveillance in asymptomatic severe AS was consistent regardless of baseline left ventricular health.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Benefit of early TAVR, compared with CS, was consistently observed regardless of whether LV health was normal or not; the abstract gives no effect estimate for this comparison.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing of intervention in asymptomatic aortic stenosis and whether LV remodelling should guide it.

title: Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic-Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients at 7 Years.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1000 patients randomised 1:1 to transfemoral TAVR or surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide intervals for components such as death (19.5% vs 16.8%), and follow-up still short of lifetime durability needs in younger patients.
appraisal.one_line: PARTNER 3 seven-year results show no significant difference between transfemoral TAVR and surgery in low-risk patients for either primary end point.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the incidence of an end-point event was 34.6% with TAVR and 37.2% with surgery (difference, -2.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -9.0 to 3.7); win ratio 1.04 (95% CI, 0.84 to 1.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised follow-up of TAVR in low-risk patients, central to lifetime management and guideline age thresholds.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with the Trilogy valve for symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (ALIGN-AR): a pivotal, multicentre, single-arm, investigational device exemption study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-arm multicentre study at 30 US centres; 1352 screened and 700 enrolled (pivotal cohort n=180; continued access cohort n=520).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design against literature-based performance goals, industry funded, high surgical risk patients only.
appraisal.one_line: ALIGN-AR pivotal single-arm study of the dedicated Trilogy valve for native aortic regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 30-day primary safety composite endpoint occurred in 168 patients (24·0% [upper 97·5% CI 27·3%]; pnon-inferiority<0·0001), meeting the performance goal. All-cause mortality occurred in 38 at 1 year (7·7% [upper 97·5% CI 10·4%]; psuperiority<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a purpose-built TAVI platform for a condition where standard devices perform poorly.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Novel Balloon-Expandable vs Contemporary Transcatheter Heart Valves in Severe Aortic Stenosis: The LANDMARK Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial, 768 participants at 31 hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: The one-year noninferiority hypothesis was introduced a posteriori and is descriptive and exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: LANDMARK one-year results show a balloon-expandable Myval valve had similar outcomes to SAPIEN or Evolut valves.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant difference in the Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from the composite endpoint at 365 days (Myval THV 87.0% vs contemporary THVs 86.9%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised device comparison informing transcatheter valve choice.

title: Physiology vs angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the FAITAVI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised superiority trial, 320 patients across 15 Italian centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small open-label trial with a borderline P value and a benefit driven mainly by all-cause mortality.
appraisal.one_line: FAITAVI found FFR-guided PCI was associated with lower 12-month MACCE than angiography-guided PCI in TAVI patients with intermediate coronary lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: FFR-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower rate of MACCE at 12 months compared with angiography-guided PCI (8.5% vs 16.0%; hazard ratio .52; 95% confidence interval .27-.99; P = .047).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on coronary revascularisation strategy in TAVI candidates, a question with little trial data.

title: Six-Year Outcomes After Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Low-Risk Patients With Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1,414 patients with attempted implantation (730 TAVR, 684 surgery).
appraisal.main_limitation: Seven-year analysis was additional and included only patients with available data at database lock.
appraisal.one_line: Six-year Evolut Low Risk results show similar mortality or disabling stroke after TAVR and surgery, with a higher reintervention rate after TAVR at seven years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 6 years, the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or disabling stroke was 23.3% for TAVR and 20.4% for surgery (difference: 2.8% [95% CI: -1.9% to 7.6%]; P = 0.43).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reintervention signal after TAVR (sHR: 1.68 [95% CI: 1.10-2.58]) bears on lifetime management in younger low-risk patients.

title: Early Surgery or Conservative Care for Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis at 10 Years.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial of early surgery versus conservative care; 145 patients randomised (73 early surgery, 72 conservative care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small single-trial sample with surgical rather than transcatheter treatment.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of a small trial in asymptomatic very severe aortic stenosis: early surgery was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality than conservative care.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 2 of 73 patients (3%) vs 17 of 72 (24%) (hazard ratio, 0.10; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.02 to 0.43; P = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data supporting early intervention in asymptomatic severe AS, relevant to TAVI timing questions.

title: Deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (PRO-TAVI): an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated multicentre randomised trial (PRO-TAVI); 466 patients (233 deferral, 233 PCI before TAVI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample with a wide interval for the rate difference.
appraisal.one_line: Deferring PCI until after TAVI was non-inferior to PCI before TAVI for a 1-year composite.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint in 56 (24%) of 233 patients vs 60 (26%) of 233 patients (rate difference -1·7% [95% CI -9·5 to 6·2]; hazard ratio 0·89 [95% CI 0·62-1·28]; p=0·0008 for non-inferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a conservative approach to CAD in TAVI candidates, a common decision with discordant guidance.

title: 10-Year Randomized Outcomes of Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Intermediate-Risk Aortic Stenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (PARTNER 2A); 1,910 randomised patients received a valve (974 TAVR, 936 surgery).
appraisal.main_limitation: Older-generation valve and differing access routes, with echocardiographic data in only a small subset.
