appraisal.one_line: Ten-year randomised results: SAPIEN XT TAVR in intermediate-risk patients was associated with lower survival than surgery, mainly in transapical or transaortic access.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause 10-year mortality with vital status sweeps was 86.1% after TAVR and 82.8% after surgery (HR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.02-1.25; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised TAVR versus surgery follow-up, relevant to durability and lifetime management.

title: Timing of PCI in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial (TAVI PCI); 986 patients (498 TAVI-first, 488 PCI-first).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a one-year horizon.
appraisal.one_line: In severe AS with coronary disease, TAVI before PCI was noninferior to PCI before TAVI at 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 105 patients (22.2%) vs 112 patients (24.2%) (risk difference, -2.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -7.4 to 3.4; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs sequencing of PCI and TAVI, alongside the PRO-TAVI deferral trial.

title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis; 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites included, with 10 963 strokes (2.1%) reported within 30 days.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with possible ascertainment bias in stroke reporting.
appraisal.one_line: National TVT Registry analysis showing stroke reporting after TAVR varies with comprehensive stroke centre designation, which matters for hospital performance metrics.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (P=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (P=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (P=NS).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests public reporting and quality metrics for TAVR stroke may be confounded by differences in stroke ascertainment between hospitals.

title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial; 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: The findings are post hoc subgroup results that the authors say need confirmation in randomized trials.
appraisal.one_line: A post hoc substudy of a randomised trial examines coronary disease extent (SYNTAX score) and outcomes after deferred versus pre-TAVR PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It suggests that the safety of deferring PCI before TAVR may not extend to complex coronary disease.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry; 466 matched pairs, median follow-up 24 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective design with residual confounding after propensity matching.
appraisal.one_line: A propensity-matched registry comparison found fewer heart failure hospitalisations with conduction system pacing than right ventricular pacing after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pacing strategy after TAVR is a frequent decision and the finding supports a randomised comparison.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Combined TAVR-PCI Versus SAVR-CABG in Patients with Aortic Stenosis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis; Fourteen studies (two randomized trials, nine cohorts, three administrative databases), 154,892 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Predominantly observational data with confounding; randomised data were too limited to confirm findings.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis separating randomised and observational evidence for TAVR plus PCI versus SAVR plus CABG, excluding overlapping populations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early mortality (odds ratio (OR) 0.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.84), and with higher mortality over 12-72 months (hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 1.28-1.49; nine observational studies).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the common decision on revascularisation in patients with aortic stenosis and coronary disease, where randomised evidence is thin.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial (DapaTAVI); 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analysis of a single trial, so the interaction is hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of DapaTAVI examining whether the effect of dapagliflozin after TAVI differs by frailty status.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests greater relative benefit of dapagliflozin after TAVI in frail patients, a group common in practice and poorly represented in trials.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide population-based cohort study; 5259 eligible patients, 292 propensity score-matched patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small matched sample and residual confounding in an observational design.
appraisal.one_line: Danish cohort study of GLP-1 receptor agonist use and outcomes after aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Generates a hypothesis for incretin-based therapy after valve replacement, a population excluded from the major cardiovascular outcome trials.

title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) in the review, four in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476).
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with a study-defined composite endpoint, and the network ranking rests on sparse direct comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analysis of randomised trials of routine PCI versus conservative management of coronary disease in patients undergoing TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the randomised evidence on revascularisation before TAVI, a contested decision in which guidelines remain cautious.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy following aortic valve intervention for aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mortality, heart failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of reports comprising one randomized trial and 11 observational studies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled estimates are almost entirely observational and prone to confounding by indication and immortal time.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review and meta-analysis of SGLT2 inhibitor use after aortic valve intervention, mostly observational data from TAVR cohorts.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.79; I²=5%; p < 0.001). The study-defined composite clinical outcome was also lower (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=57%; p = 0.005).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Identifies a plausible post-TAVI pharmacotherapy question that only a randomised trial can settle.
